MCF-GOV-001.objective: Establish one approved charter that defines who directs, oversees and is accountable for assurance of each in-scope Capability Instance, which decision questions the programme serves, and the limits of reliance on AIDCF conclusions.
MCF-GOV-001.requirement: The governing body shall approve an assurance governance charter that names the in-scope Capability Instances, the accountable executive, the assurance programme lead, the decision authority and the oversight committee; states the decision questions served and the intended users of conclusions; defines the programme model (self-assessment, co-sourced, second-party or independent provider); and states that AIDCF conclusions do not replace engineering, statutory or safety approval and are not certification. The accountable executive shall review the charter at no more than the governance charter review interval and after any change of ownership, organisation or programme model, and shall record the outcome of each review.
MCF-GOV-001.unknownEffect: US3 Material: control result UNKNOWN; CG-13 gate-level evaluation records the gap; decision capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a named condition to evidence charter approval

MCF-GOV-002.objective: Ensure that every consequential decision affecting the AI capability and its assurance (risk acceptance, gate disposition, Assurance Decision, emergency load action, test authorisation, exception approval) has a defined, delegated decision right that is used as designed, including in emergency states.
MCF-GOV-002.requirement: The accountable executive shall maintain a decision-rights matrix that, for each decision class affecting an in-scope Capability Instance, names the role holding the decision right, its financial or risk limits, the escalation route, the delegation and sub-delegation rules, and the emergency decision rights that apply when the normal holder is unavailable. The assurance programme lead shall ensure that workflow and approval systems enforce the matrix, and that every decision in the sample population was taken by a role holding the right at the time it was taken.
MCF-GOV-002.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-13 Gate Result UNKNOWN; decision capped at LIMITED until the decision-rights evidence is produced

MCF-GOV-003.requirement: The governing body shall constitute an assurance oversight committee with written terms of reference, quorum and membership that includes at least one member independent of the operating line. The committee chair shall ensure that the committee meets at no more than the oversight meeting interval, receives at every meeting the current gate register, UNKNOWN register (US3 and above), findings register and overdue action list for each in-scope Capability Instance, records challenge and decisions in minutes, and tracks its own actions to closure.

MCF-GOV-004.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall appoint a methodology owner who shall maintain a controlled methodology baseline listing the AIDCF artifact versions (including AIDCF-007A, AIDCF-008, AIDCF-009 and AIDCF-010), the capability profile, scoring version and every approved local tailoring, each with rationale and approval. The methodology owner shall ensure that assessment tools and templates are configured to that baseline and that every report declares the baseline version actually used.

MCF-GOV-005.requirement: The accountable executive shall maintain a RACI that assigns, for each in-scope process (capability management, assurance, evidence, change, incident, recovery, provider management), exactly one Accountable role and the Responsible, Consulted and Informed roles across owner, operator, tenants and providers. The assurance programme lead shall reconcile the RACI to current appointments and to contractual responsibility clauses at least at the RACI reconciliation interval and after every organisational or contract change.
MCF-GOV-005.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-13 Gate Result UNKNOWN; decision capped at LIMITED

MCF-GOV-006.requirement: The capability owner shall ensure that each Required Function and each material Dependency linked to an in-scope Service Outcome has exactly one accountable owner recorded in the assurance graph, that the owner holds the decision right to commit resources and to authorise degraded-state actions for that function, and that cross-organisational functions (for example utility supply, facility water, network carriers, cloud control planes) have both an internal accountable owner and a named counterparty contact. MCF-GOV-007.requirement: The accountable executive shall define risk-acceptance authority levels linked to the risk appetite (MCF-GOV-014) and impact tolerances (MCF-CAP-010). The assurance programme lead shall ensure that no acceptance of a risk that would cause a CRITICAL control or gate to be relied upon is recorded without the decision authority's approval, and that expired acceptances revert to open Findings.

MCF-GOV-008.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall appoint an evidence lead who shall assign a custodian role to each evidence repository and each Evidence Package, define who may read, add, alter, export, redact or destroy evidence, and ensure that every custody event defined in AIDCF-008 (transfer, access, export, alteration, redaction, retention action) is recorded. MCF-GOV-011.requirement: The policy owner shall operate an exception process in which each exception records the requirement deviated from, affected Capability Instances, Service Outcomes, controls and gates, the risk assessment, compensating measures, approver, expiry and closure criteria. Exceptions affecting a gate-critical control shall be approved by the decision authority. The assurance programme lead shall ensure that the exception register is an input to every assessment and that expired exceptions are escalated to the oversight committee.

MCF-GOV-012.objective: Ensure that documents used to operate and assure the capability are controlled through creation, review, approval, publication, supersession and withdrawal, so that the version at the point of use is the approved current version.

MCF-GOV-013.objective: Ensure that a risk-based assurance plan determines which Capability Instances, Service Outcomes, claim types and gates are assessed, at what Assurance Level, by whom and when, so that assurance effort follows consequence and change rather than convenience.
MCF-GOV-013.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall prepare, and the oversight committee shall approve, an assurance plan for each planning period that, for each in-scope Capability Instance, states the decision questions, target Assurance Level (AL0-AL6), claim types and gates to be evaluated, assessment type, provider model, resourcing and schedule, and the rationale linking depth to criticality (MCF-CAP-009) and planned change (MCF-CAP-023). The programme lead shall record and approve deviations from the plan.

MCF-GOV-014.objective: Ensure that the organisation's stated risk appetite is translated into measurable limits for the AI capability (for example tolerated outcome interruption, tolerated loss of training progress, tolerated degraded-state duration) that drive impact tolerances, risk acceptance and decision conditions.
MCF-GOV-014.requirement: The governing body shall approve a risk appetite statement covering service continuity, safety, data integrity and dependency concentration for the AI capability. MCF-GOV-015.objective: Ensure that critical gates are evaluated, disposed and reported under governance that prevents them from being averaged away, re-scoped or overridden, and that every FAIL or UNKNOWN Gate Result reaches the decision authority with its controlling effect.
MCF-GOV-015.requirement: The decision authority shall maintain a gate register for each in-scope Capability Instance recording, for every gate CG-01 to CG-15, applicability, CRITICAL control results, evidence sufficiency against the gate floor, Gate Result, controlling effect on the decision and closure criteria. The assurance programme lead shall ensure that Gate Results are computed by the roll-up rule of AIDCF-010, that no Gate Result is changed except by reassessment, and that APPROVED_NA is granted only by the decision authority with a boundary rationale.

MCF-GOV-016.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall ensure that every Assurance Decision supporting a material decision question is subject, before issue, to independent review by a reviewer who did not prepare or perform the assessment, has no conflict under MCF-GOV-021 and holds the competence defined in MCF-GOV-023. The independent reviewer shall record challenges, responses and dispositions, and shall have authority to withhold their concurrence. The programme lead shall periodically test review effectiveness by reperformance or by seeded-defect review.

MCF-GOV-017.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain a stakeholder obligation register identifying each obligation that constrains an in-scope Capability Instance (for example contracted availability, data residency, grid connection conditions, water abstraction limits, noise and emission permits, insurance warranties), its source document, owner and the Service Outcome, tolerance or operating constraint into which it is translated.

MCF-GOV-018.objective: Ensure that changes in law, regulation, permits and mandatory standards affecting the AI capability (energy, water, emissions, safety, data and critical-infrastructure regimes) are detected, assessed for impact and actioned in time.
MCF-GOV-018.requirement: The compliance owner shall operate a regulatory monitoring process covering each jurisdiction in which in-scope infrastructure is located, record each relevant change with an impact assessment against Service Outcomes, controls and obligations, assign actions, and report material changes to the oversight committee. Changes affecting life safety, hazardous energy or reporting duties shall be escalated within the regulatory escalation time.

MCF-GOV-019.requirement: The commercial owner shall ensure that each customer or tenant commitment concerning availability, performance, integrity, capacity or recovery of an in-scope Capability Instance is recorded with its metric definition, measurement method and exclusions, and is reconciled by the capability owner to the approved Service Outcomes and tolerances before signature and after every change to either. Commitments exceeding approved Service Outcomes shall be approved by the accountable executive with a recorded risk acceptance.

MCF-GOV-020.requirement: The decision authority shall approve every external communication that conveys an AIDCF assurance conclusion before release. The communications owner shall ensure that each such communication uses the controlled decision language of AIDCF-012, identifies the Capability Instance, scope, period and limitations, includes every gate FAIL and US4/US5 UNKNOWN relevant to the audience, contains no prohibited claim (certification, accreditation, universal safety or resilience), and is withdrawn or corrected when the underlying decision is suspended, withdrawn or superseded.

MCF-GOV-021.objective: Ensure that conflicts of interest affecting assessors, reviewers, specialists and decision authorities (financial, self-review, familiarity, advocacy, intimidation) are declared, evaluated and safeguarded before work begins and throughout the engagement.
MCF-GOV-021.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall require every assessor, reviewer, specialist and decision authority to declare interests before assignment and on any change, shall evaluate each declared or identified threat (self-review, self-interest, familiarity, advocacy, intimidation), and shall apply and record a safeguard or exclusion. The programme lead shall prohibit outcome-contingent fees for assurance conclusions and shall exclude from assessment any person who designed, built, operates or advised on the control under assessment within the cooling-off period.

MCF-GOV-022.objective: Ensure that the organisational and reporting independence of the assessment function matches the reliance placed on its conclusions, so that preparation, performance, review and decision remain separable.
MCF-GOV-022.requirement: The governing body shall define the independence level required for each class of intended reliance (management use, customer reliance, regulatory or financing reliance). The assurance programme lead shall ensure that for each engagement the assessment team's reporting line, provider model and separation of preparation, performance, review and decision meet the required level, and that the actual independence level is stated in the Assurance Statement.

MCF-GOV-023.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall maintain a competence framework for each role and domain (aligned to AIDCF-011 Part IX), a register recording each person's evidenced competence and its currency, and an assignment check confirming that every engagement assignment matches recorded competence. Where competence is not available internally, the lead shall engage a specialist under recorded reliance with scope and responsibility.

MCF-GOV-024.requirement: The decision authority shall maintain an appeal and challenge procedure that defines who may challenge, grounds, time limits, the impartial reviewer, evidence required, and possible outcomes. The decision authority shall ensure that every challenge is logged, decided by a person not involved in the challenged result, and that the original result, the challenge and the outcome are all preserved, with any change made only by reassessment.

MCF-CAP-001.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain a capability register in which each Capability Instance has a unique identifier, a description of the AI work it delivers (training, fine-tuning, inference, data preparation), its physical and logical location (site, hall, pods, clusters), its tenancy model, its lifecycle status, its accountable owner, its Service Outcomes and its current ArchitectureSnapshot reference. MCF-CAP-002.requirement: The accountable executive shall appoint, for each Capability Instance, one capability owner with documented authority over the Service Outcomes, impact tolerances, risk acceptance within delegated limits, and the commitment of facility, platform and provider resources needed to meet them. The capability owner shall be identified in the capability register, the RACI and the decision-rights matrix, and a deputy shall be named for EMERGENCY and RECOVERY states.

MCF-CAP-003.requirement: The capability owner shall define lifecycle status values and transition criteria for Capability Instances, shall record each status transition with date, approver and the evidence that the transition criteria were met, and shall not transition an instance to in-service until commissioning acceptance (MCF-CAP-022) is recorded. MCF-POW-019.requirement: The electrical engineer shall define the ride-through envelope for each load class (IT, CDU and pump drives, chillers, controls), including source transfers (UPS to bypass, static transfer switch, ATS, generator synchronisation) and grid dips. The facility owner shall verify by commissioning and periodic transfer tests that loads remain online for transfers within the envelope, shall ensure mechanical loads not on UPS restart automatically within the thermal time constant, and shall document compliance with connection-agreement ride-through requirements.
MCF-POW-019.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-05 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

MCF-POW-020.objective: Demonstrate that UPS, BESS, generators and the grid connection remain stable under the load steps and synchronous power oscillations produced by large accelerator clusters (collective compute/communication phases, job start and stop, checkpoint pauses and failure-driven drops), and that these dynamics are bounded within the capability of every source.
MCF-POW-020.requirement: The facility owner shall characterise the power dynamics of each AI cluster (step magnitude, ramp rate, oscillation amplitude and frequency band), using measured data at sub-second resolution or the accelerator vendor's specified behaviour, and shall verify that UPS rectifier and inverter controls, BESS, generator governors and voltage regulators, and the grid connection tolerate them without instability, protective trips or breach of connection limits. Where they do not, the facility owner shall apply mitigation (accelerator power-smoothing or ramp-limit features, workload scheduling, energy-storage buffering) and shall verify it by test, including a load-step test on generator supply.
MCF-POW-020.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-05 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

MCF-POW-021.objective: Ensure the electrical power monitoring system observes every critical node with accurate, time-synchronised data and alarms, functions independently of the systems it monitors, and is configured and protected as a critical control system.
MCF-POW-021.requirement: The facility operator shall instrument every utility incomer, generator, UPS, STS, critical switchboard, busway and representative rack PDU with metering connected to the EPMS, shall synchronise device clocks to the declared accuracy for sequence-of-events analysis, shall configure alarms per an approved alarm philosophy, and shall power the EPMS and its network from protected supplies. The facility operator shall maintain the EPMS configuration under change control and its access under SEC controls.
MCF-POW-021.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-07 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

MCF-POW-022.objective: Ensure electrical assets are maintained at intervals and to scopes that keep their reliability and safety within the assumptions of the design and resilience analysis, without maintenance itself introducing unmanaged risk.
MCF-POW-022.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a maintenance programme for each electrical asset class (switchgear, transformers, UPS, batteries, generators, ATS/STS, busway, PDUs, protection relays) with scopes and intervals based on manufacturer requirements and recognised maintenance practice, shall complete maintenance on time, and shall record deferrals with risk assessment and approval.
MCF-POW-022.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-05.

MCF-POW-023.objective: Ensure that every planned and emergency switching operation on critical distribution is performed to an approved, verified procedure by authorised persons, with hazardous energy controlled, so that switching neither injures people nor drops critical load.
MCF-POW-023.requirement: The electrical duty holder shall require a method of procedure (MOP) for every planned switching operation on critical distribution, prepared from the current single-line diagram, checked by a second authorised person, and executed with step verification. The electrical duty holder shall maintain emergency operating procedures for foreseeable failures, shall apply lockout/tagout and permit-to-work for isolation, and shall authorise persons for switching by competence assessment.
MCF-POW-023.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

MCF-POW-024.objective: Demonstrate that after a total loss of power the site can be restored from a dead state, in a safe and dependency-correct sequence (controls, cooling, then IT), within the declared recovery time, and that AI workloads can resume.
MCF-POW-024.requirement: The facility owner shall maintain a black-start and restoration plan that defines the restoration sequence, the dependencies of each step (control power, EPMS/BMS availability, cooling restart, battery recharge limits, inrush and staged load pick-up on generator), the authority to proceed, and the hand-over to IT for workload restart. The facility owner shall exercise the plan at the declared interval, either by a full integrated test or by staged tests that together cover every step, and shall measure time to each milestone.
MCF-POW-024.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-10 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

MCF-THM-001.objective: Establish an authoritative, versioned model of the heat that each fault domain must reject, split by heat-removal path (air, direct-to-chip liquid, rear-door, immersion), so that every downstream capacity, redundancy and recovery claim is tested against a defensible demand figure rather than nameplate or average IT power.
MCF-THM-001.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall maintain a versioned heat-load model for each Capability Instance that states, per hall, row, rack group and CDU or air-handling fault domain, the design and peak heat load in kW, the liquid-capture ratio by platform, residual heat to air, and the transient load profile of synchronous AI training. The facility owner shall approve the model and shall not accept capacity claims that are not traceable to the current model version.
MCF-THM-001.unknownEffect: US3 Material: capacity controls MCF-THM-002/003 cannot be rated CONFORMING against an unverified demand; decision condition recorded

MCF-THM-002.objective: Demonstrate that the installed and commissioned capacity of every stage of the heat-removal path (air, TCS, CDU, FWS, heat rejection) meets the current heat-load model at design conditions, so that the facility can actually remove the heat it is declared to support.
MCF-THM-002.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall demonstrate, for each heat-removal stage and fault domain, that commissioned capacity at design ambient and design supply temperatures is not less than the design heat load from MCF-THM-001 plus the approved margin. The facility operator shall hold the commissioning records and shall not admit IT load beyond the demonstrated capacity of the weakest stage in the path.
MCF-THM-002.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 Gate Result becomes UNKNOWN for the affected fault domains; decision ceiling per CG-06

MCF-THM-003.objective: Ensure heat removal remains within the IT inlet and coolant envelopes when any single credible component, path or controller is lost, during maintenance, and through power-event transients (utility loss, UPS transfer, generator start, chiller restart).
MCF-THM-003.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall define the declared redundancy (for example N+1, 2N) for each heat-removal stage and shall demonstrate that, with the largest single unit or path out of service, capacity meets design load. The facility owner shall demonstrate thermal ride-through: that pumps, CDUs and controls needed to keep coolant moving are on continuous power, and that thermal storage or ride-through margin keeps TCS supply and IT inlet temperatures within limits until chillers or heat rejection restart.
MCF-THM-003.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for affected fault domains; decision ≤ LIMITED until ride-through is evidenced

MCF-THM-004.objective: Ensure heat-rejection and economiser capacity is rated at the site's extreme design ambient conditions, including projected climate change, so that capacity claims hold through heatwaves and high wet-bulb periods.
MCF-THM-004.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall define design ambient dry-bulb and wet-bulb conditions from a stated climatic data source and return period, shall derate chillers, dry coolers and cooling towers to those conditions, and shall review the derating annually against observed extremes. The facility operator shall monitor available heat-rejection capacity against load during high-ambient periods and shall invoke load-management procedures before capacity is exceeded.
MCF-THM-004.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for high-ambient states; decision ceiling applied to EMERGENCY/peak-season claims

MCF-THM-005.objective: Ensure cold supply air reaches IT inlets at the required temperature and volume without bypass or recirculation, including the residual air-side heat from liquid-cooled racks.
MCF-THM-005.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain an airflow management regime (blanking, brush grommets, cable cut-out sealing, floor-tile or supply-diffuser placement, fan-wall or CRAH control) and shall verify by periodic measurement that IT inlet temperatures at the top, middle and bottom of sampled racks remain within the declared envelope and that bypass and recirculation are within declared limits.
MCF-THM-005.unknownEffect: US3 Material: air-side adequacy uncertain; condition recorded against CG-06 supporting evaluation

MCF-THM-006.objective: Ensure hot-aisle or cold-aisle containment, chimney cabinets or rear-door heat exchangers are installed and maintained as designed so that supply and exhaust air streams remain separated, and that containment does not compromise fire detection, suppression or egress.
MCF-THM-006.requirement: The facility operator shall install and maintain containment in accordance with the approved design, shall reconcile the as-built containment (doors, roof panels, end-of-row doors, rear-door heat exchangers) with the design, and shall demonstrate that fire detection and suppression coverage inside containment and the release of drop-away or fusible panels have been accepted by the fire-safety authority.
MCF-THM-006.unknownEffect: US3 Material: air separation unverified; CG-06 supporting; any fire-safety acceptance gap escalated to CG-04 evaluation

MCF-THM-007.objective: Ensure computer-room air handlers, fan walls and in-row coolers deliver the air-side capacity required by the heat-load model, with declared redundancy, at the actual chilled-water or facility-water supply temperature.
MCF-THM-007.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a unit schedule for air handlers and in-row coolers stating sensible capacity at the actual entering-water and return-air conditions, and shall demonstrate that each air-cooling zone meets residual air heat with the declared redundancy. The thermal engineering authority shall re-rate capacity when supply water temperature or return-air setpoints change.
MCF-THM-007.unknownEffect: US3 Material: zone air-side capacity uncertain; CG-06 supporting evaluation required

MCF-THM-008.objective: Ensure air temperature, humidity and differential pressure are measured at points that represent IT inlet conditions, with alarm thresholds that give operators time to act before IT thermal limits or throttling are reached.
MCF-THM-008.requirement: The facility operator shall deploy and maintain air-side sensors at IT inlet positions (not only at return air), with calibrated accuracy, defined alarm thresholds tiered below the IT envelope limits, and alarm routing to a staffed function. The facility operator shall review alarm performance, sensor coverage and nuisance alarms at least quarterly.
MCF-THM-008.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: confidence ceiling CONF-2 for air-side operating claims

MCF-THM-009.objective: Ensure the direct-to-chip liquid-cooling architecture (cold plates, manifolds, technology cooling system, CDUs and facility water interface) is designed to the accelerator OEM's coolant, temperature, flow, pressure and wetted-material requirements and to an explicit facility water class.
MCF-THM-009.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall document a direct-to-chip design basis stating: the TCS fluid, supply temperature range, minimum flow per rack and per cold plate, maximum pressure and differential pressure, filtration, wetted materials, and the ASHRAE liquid-cooling W-class of the facility water system at the CDU interface. The facility owner shall obtain written OEM confirmation that the design basis meets the platform requirements and shall maintain a TCS/FWS P&ID.
MCF-THM-009.unknownEffect: US3 Material: liquid-cooling design adequacy uncertain; CG-06 supporting; downstream CDU and loop controls conditioned

MCF-THM-010.objective: Demonstrate that coolant distribution units deliver the required heat transfer, flow and supply temperature to every served rack under design load, with declared redundancy of pumps, heat exchangers and power supplies.
MCF-THM-010.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall demonstrate, by commissioning or periodic test, that each CDU group delivers design heat transfer at design FWS temperature with the declared pump and heat-exchanger redundancy, and that pump failover maintains flow without TCS supply temperature leaving the OEM limit. The facility operator shall not connect racks to a CDU group beyond its demonstrated capacity.
MCF-THM-010.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for racks served by untested CDU groups

MCF-THM-011.objective: Ensure the technology cooling system (secondary loop) maintains pressure, flow, temperature and fluid inventory within limits, is pressure-tested, and has no unmanaged single points of failure between CDU and cold plate.
MCF-THM-011.requirement: The facility operator shall monitor TCS supply and return temperature, differential pressure, flow, system pressure and make-up/fill volume continuously, shall pressure-test new and modified TCS pipework before fill, and shall investigate any unexplained make-up volume. The thermal engineering authority shall maintain a single-point-of-failure analysis of the TCS from CDU to manifold to cold plate.
MCF-THM-011.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for loops with unverified integrity

MCF-THM-012.objective: Ensure quick-disconnect couplings between manifolds and IT are specified, compatible, connected, inspected and replaced under control, because they are the most frequently operated wetted joints and a common leak and flow-restriction source.
MCF-THM-012.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a register of quick-disconnect coupling types and compatibility by platform, shall perform connect/disconnect only under a documented procedure by trained staff with drip containment, and shall inspect and replace couplings and seals on a defined interval or cycle count. The AI platform operator shall not install IT with couplings outside the register.
MCF-THM-012.unknownEffect: US3 Material: leak initiation risk unbounded; supports CG-06 and CG-04 evaluation

MCF-THM-013.objective: Demonstrate that chillers (where present) deliver required capacity at design condenser conditions with declared redundancy, restart quickly after power interruption, and that refrigerant hazards are controlled.
MCF-THM-013.requirement: The facility operator shall demonstrate chiller capacity at design condenser conditions with the declared redundancy, shall evidence restart-to-capacity time after power interruption, and shall maintain refrigerant inventory, leak detection, machinery-room ventilation and safety classification records in accordance with the applicable refrigeration safety standard.
MCF-THM-013.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for chilled-water-dependent paths; refrigerant safety gaps escalated to CG-04

MCF-THM-014.objective: Ensure final heat-rejection equipment (cooling towers, adiabatic or dry coolers) operates at the required capacity, is protected against fouling, freezing, recirculation and fan or spray failures, and is maintained to preserve capacity.
MCF-THM-014.requirement: The facility operator shall operate and maintain heat-rejection units to preserve capacity at design ambient, shall monitor approach temperature and fan/pump status per unit, shall protect against freezing and hot-air recirculation, and shall record fouling and coil-cleaning interventions. Where evaporative or adiabatic systems are used, the facility operator shall implement MCF-THM-018 water treatment.
MCF-THM-014.unknownEffect: US3 Material: heat-rejection capacity condition recorded; CG-06 supporting

MCF-THM-015.objective: Ensure evaporative and adiabatic heat rejection, and loop make-up, can continue through loss or restriction of mains water supply for the declared autonomy period.
MCF-THM-015.requirement: The facility owner shall determine water consumption at design ambient and peak load, shall provide on-site storage or alternative supply for the declared water autonomy, and shall document the dependency on the water utility, including restriction scenarios and drought orders. The facility operator shall test the switchover to stored or alternative water and shall monitor stored volume.
MCF-THM-015.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for water-dependent heat rejection under EMERGENCY states

MCF-THM-016.objective: Make explicit every dependency of the heat-removal path on external or shared resources (water, power, controls, district systems, shared plant with other tenants) and the common modes that could remove several redundant trains at once.
MCF-THM-016.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall maintain a heat-rejection dependency map from IT heat source to final heat sink, identifying shared headers, common controllers, common power boards, shared water supplies, third-party plant and heat-reuse interfaces, and shall record the treatment and owner of each common mode. The facility owner shall ensure heat-reuse or district-energy interfaces cannot reduce heat-rejection capacity below design load.
MCF-THM-016.unknownEffect: US3 Material: hidden common mode possible; referred to CG-03 and CG-09 evaluation

MCF-THM-017.objective: Ensure every coolant and immersion fluid is compatible with all wetted materials and IT components, is safe to handle, and that its hazards (toxicity, flammability, environmental, pressure) are identified and controlled.
MCF-THM-017.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall specify each coolant (for example propylene-glycol solution, treated water, dielectric immersion fluid) with its composition, inhibitor package, approved wetted materials and OEM approval, and shall obtain and act upon the safety data sheet. The facility owner shall ensure fluid handling, storage, spill response and disposal arrangements are in place and accepted by the site safety authority.
MCF-THM-017.unknownEffect: US3 Material: corrosion or fluid-hazard risk unbounded; CG-04 supporting evaluation

MCF-THM-018.objective: Maintain the chemistry, cleanliness and microbiological quality of TCS, FWS and condenser water so that cold plates do not foul, corrosion is controlled, and evaporative systems do not present a legionella risk to people.
MCF-THM-018.requirement: The facility operator shall implement a water-quality programme with sampling frequencies and limits for each loop (pH, conductivity, inhibitor level, glycol concentration, suspended solids, microbiological counts), shall maintain filtration to the OEM rating, and shall act on out-of-limit results within defined times. Where evaporative cooling towers or adiabatic systems exist, the facility owner shall maintain a legionella risk assessment and written control scheme under the applicable regulation, reviewed by a competent person.
MCF-THM-018.unknownEffect: US4 Critical where evaporative systems exist (CG-04 life safety); otherwise US3 Material for CG-06

MCF-THM-019.objective: Ensure liquid leaks from TCS, FWS, rear-door heat exchangers and immersion tanks are detected quickly and located precisely enough to isolate the right section before liquid reaches energised equipment or spreads beyond its fault domain.
MCF-THM-019.requirement: The facility operator shall install leak detection (rope/cable sensors, spot sensors, CDU and rack-level detection, flow/pressure-based detection) covering every wetted zone above or adjacent to IT and electrical equipment, shall route alarms to a staffed function with locational information, and shall functionally test detection at defined intervals. The thermal engineering authority shall define detection coverage and response time requirements per zone.
MCF-THM-019.unknownEffect: US3 Material: leak detection effectiveness uncertain; CG-09 and CG-04 supporting evaluation

MCF-THM-020.objective: Ensure a detected leak can be isolated to the smallest practicable section, the released liquid is contained and drained away from energised equipment, and the remaining cooling capacity is preserved, so that a leak remains within its fault domain.
MCF-THM-020.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall design isolation valves, drip trays, bunding and drainage so that a leak at any credible point can be isolated to a defined fault domain and drained without reaching electrical equipment outside that domain. The facility operator shall maintain isolation procedures, exercise valves, and demonstrate isolation of a representative section while adjacent sections continue cooling.
MCF-THM-020.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-09 UNKNOWN for liquid-leak containment

MCF-THM-021.objective: Ensure cooling controls (CDU controllers, BMS sequences, chiller plant managers, pump and valve PID loops) remain stable under rapid AI load swings, fail to a safe cooling state on controller or network loss, and cannot be changed without control.
MCF-THM-021.requirement: The controls engineering authority shall document control sequences and fail-safe states for each cooling controller, shall demonstrate stability of temperature and pressure loops under step load changes representative of synchronous training, and shall demonstrate that loss of controller, sensor or controls network leaves pumps running and valves in a safe position. The facility operator shall manage controller configuration under change control with version-controlled backups.
MCF-THM-021.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-07 UNKNOWN for cooling controls

MCF-THM-022.objective: Ensure the sensors that drive cooling control and alarming (temperature, pressure, flow, leak, level) are accurate, calibrated, redundant where control-critical, and that implausible or failed readings are detected before they mislead control or operators.
MCF-THM-022.requirement: The facility operator shall identify control-critical sensors, shall calibrate them at defined intervals, shall provide redundancy or plausibility checks (cross-sensor comparison, rate-of-change, stuck-value detection) for control-critical points, and shall configure controllers to a safe default on sensor failure.
MCF-THM-022.unknownEffect: US3 Material: telemetry reliability reduced; dependent operating claims capped at CONF-2

MCF-THM-023.objective: Ensure planned maintenance on cooling plant (CDU servicing, filter changes, valve replacement, chiller overhaul, loop drain-down) is carried out without unplanned loss of cooling, with declared residual redundancy and safe isolation of pressurised fluid systems.
MCF-THM-023.requirement: The facility operator shall plan cooling maintenance with a documented method statement stating residual capacity and redundancy during the work, required IT load limits, isolation and lock-out points, and back-out steps; shall coordinate with the AI platform operator where IT load must be reduced; and shall record post-maintenance return-to-service checks.
MCF-THM-023.unknownEffect: US3 Material: maintenance-state continuity uncertain; CG-06 and CG-14 supporting

MCF-THM-024.objective: Ensure that after loss of cooling or power, the heat-removal path is restored in the right order (power, controls, pumps, heat rejection, CDUs) and IT load is readmitted in steps that do not exceed recovering capacity or trigger repeated thermal trips.
MCF-THM-024.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a thermal recovery procedure defining restart sequence, prerequisites, hold points, verification criteria (flow, TCS supply temperature, leak checks) and staged IT readmission limits agreed with the AI platform operator, and shall exercise it at a defined interval. The facility owner shall define the thermal recovery time objective for each fault domain.
MCF-THM-024.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-10 UNKNOWN for thermal recovery

MCF-ENV-001.objective: Demonstrate that air inlet temperatures at IT equipment and liquid coolant supply temperatures to cold plates or immersion tanks stay within the declared envelope and rate-of-change limits in all declared operating states, measured where the equipment experiences them.
MCF-ENV-001.requirement: The facility operator shall declare, for each hall and liquid loop, the environmental class (ASHRAE air-cooling class and liquid-cooling W class, or OEM envelope where more restrictive) and shall measure inlet air temperature at representative rack inlets and coolant supply temperature at the technology cooling system interface. The facility operator shall alarm excursions and rates of change outside the envelope, investigate them, and report excursion time per hall at the declared interval.
MCF-ENV-001.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-06, CG-08.

MCF-ENV-002.objective: Ensure moisture conditions avoid condensation on liquid-cooled components and pipework, electrostatic discharge risk at low humidity, and corrosion acceleration at high humidity.
MCF-ENV-002.requirement: The facility operator shall control and monitor dew point and relative humidity in IT spaces within the declared envelope and shall maintain coolant supply temperatures above room dew point by the declared margin wherever uninsulated liquid-cooling components are exposed to room air. The facility operator shall alarm when the margin is lost and shall define the response.
MCF-ENV-002.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-06.

MCF-ENV-003.objective: Ensure airborne particulate and gaseous contaminants are controlled so that hardware reliability is not degraded, particularly where economisation or high airflow increases outdoor air exposure.
MCF-ENV-003.requirement: The facility operator shall measure gaseous corrosivity by copper and silver reactivity coupons or real-time monitors and particulate cleanliness at the declared interval, shall maintain filtration to the declared grade, and shall act when the severity level exceeds the declared class, including restricting economiser operation during external pollution events.
MCF-ENV-003.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-08.

MCF-ENV-004.objective: Ensure vibration and sound levels do not degrade storage and IT equipment (including acoustic damage to hard disk drives during gaseous suppression discharge), do not exceed occupational noise limits in dense halls, and comply with boundary noise limits in permits.
MCF-ENV-004.requirement: The facility owner shall specify suppression discharge nozzles and agent release rates that keep sound pressure at storage equipment below the storage OEM threshold, shall measure occupational noise exposure in halls and plant rooms against regulatory action values and provide hearing protection and signage where exceeded, and shall demonstrate that site boundary noise from generators, heat rejection and transformers complies with planning or permit limits.
MCF-ENV-004.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-08.

MCF-ENV-005.objective: Ensure power usage effectiveness is measured according to ISO/IEC 30134-2 with a declared measurement category, boundary and period, so that reported values are comparable, traceable and not distorted by metering gaps or boundary choices.
MCF-ENV-005.requirement: The energy manager shall calculate PUE as annual total facility energy divided by annual IT equipment energy per ISO/IEC 30134-2, shall declare the measurement category and the metering points used for IT energy, shall include all energy sources (grid, on-site generation, fuel for generators), and shall report the value with category, period and data completeness.
MCF-ENV-005.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-006.objective: Ensure energy consumed by shared infrastructure is allocated to tenants, clusters or services by a documented and metered method, so that per-capability energy and emissions are defensible.
MCF-ENV-006.requirement: The energy manager shall define an allocation method for shared facility energy (cooling, losses, lighting, offices) to tenants or AI clusters, shall base allocation on sub-metered data wherever metering exists, and shall report unallocated energy below the declared threshold.
MCF-ENV-006.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-007.objective: Ensure facility efficiency is characterised across the load range actually experienced by AI deployments (partial occupancy during ramp-up, variable training load) and that heat reuse, where claimed, is measured.
MCF-ENV-007.requirement: The energy manager shall report PUE or partial PUE at the declared IT load points, shall document the efficiency curves of major equipment (UPS, chillers, CDUs) at those points, and, where heat is exported for reuse, shall measure exported heat energy and report the energy reuse factor per ISO/IEC 30134-6.
MCF-ENV-007.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-008.objective: Ensure that efficiency measures (UPS eco-mode, raised supply temperatures, reduced running redundant units, economiser hours, power capping) are evaluated for their effect on power and thermal resilience before adoption, so that efficiency gains do not silently consume resilience.
MCF-ENV-008.requirement: The facility owner shall require a resilience impact assessment for every efficiency measure affecting power or cooling, reviewed by the electrical and mechanical engineers responsible for CG-05 and CG-06 evidence, stating the effect on transfer behaviour, ride-through, thermal ride-through time and redundancy in each declared operating state. The facility owner shall approve the measure under change control only when the assessment shows declared tolerances are still met.
MCF-ENV-008.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-05, CG-06, CG-14.

MCF-ENV-009.objective: Ensure water supplies for heat rejection, adiabatic cooling and humidification are identified, of controlled quality, and treated to prevent scaling, corrosion, biofouling and Legionella risk.
MCF-ENV-009.requirement: The facility operator shall document each water source (mains, borehole, reclaimed), its contracted or permitted volume and quality, and shall operate a water treatment programme with the declared monitoring frequency for chemistry and microbiology, including a Legionella risk assessment and control scheme for evaporative systems, reviewed by a competent person.
MCF-ENV-009.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-06, CG-04.

MCF-ENV-010.objective: Ensure water usage effectiveness is measured per ISO/IEC 30134-9 with complete metering of site water inputs, so that water claims are comparable and traceable.
MCF-ENV-010.requirement: The energy and sustainability manager shall calculate WUE as annual site water use divided by annual IT equipment energy per ISO/IEC 30134-9, shall meter every water input, shall state which uses are included (heat rejection, humidification, domestic) and shall report data completeness. Where source-side water (water used in electricity generation) is reported, the basis shall be stated separately.
MCF-ENV-010.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-011.objective: Demonstrate that the site maintains heat-rejection capacity for the declared outcomes when water supply is restricted or interrupted, using storage, alternative sources or dry operation with a known capacity penalty.
MCF-ENV-011.requirement: The facility owner shall maintain a water scarcity response plan stating on-site storage autonomy at design-day consumption, alternative sources, the capacity of heat rejection in water-free or reduced-water mode at design ambient, and the load-reduction actions if that capacity is below the declared IT load. The facility operator shall exercise switchover to reduced-water mode at the declared interval.
MCF-ENV-011.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-06, CG-03.

MCF-ENV-012.objective: Ensure discharges of cooling-tower blowdown, treated water, glycol and stormwater comply with permits and that accidental releases of coolant, fuel or fire-water are contained.
MCF-ENV-012.requirement: The facility operator shall hold and comply with discharge consents for trade effluent and surface water, shall monitor discharge quality at the declared frequency, shall provide interceptors and containment for fuel, glycol and potentially contaminated fire-fighting water, and shall report permit breaches to the regulator as required.
MCF-ENV-012.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-013.objective: Ensure the organisational and operational boundary for greenhouse gas accounting of AI capability is defined consistently with the GHG Protocol, including colocation, leased and on-site generation emissions, so that carbon usage effectiveness and footprint claims are well-founded.
MCF-ENV-013.requirement: The sustainability manager shall define the consolidation approach (operational or financial control, or equity share), the Scope 1 (generator fuel, refrigerant leakage), Scope 2 (location-based and market-based) and relevant Scope 3 categories (purchased hardware, construction, upstream fuel) for each site, shall state exclusions with justification, and shall calculate CUE per ISO/IEC 30134-8 on the declared basis.
MCF-ENV-013.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-014.objective: Ensure claims of renewable or carbon-free electricity are backed by retired energy attribute certificates or contractual instruments matched to consumption by the declared temporal and geographic rules, without double counting.
MCF-ENV-014.requirement: The sustainability manager shall hold evidence of cancellation or retirement of energy attribute certificates (for example guarantees of origin or RECs) or of contractual instruments (PPAs) for every claimed MWh, shall match them to consumption by the declared temporal granularity (annual or hourly) and market boundary, and shall ensure no instrument is claimed by another party.
MCF-ENV-014.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-015.objective: Ensure embodied carbon and material data for buildings, plant and AI hardware are collected on a consistent life-cycle basis so that lifecycle footprint and refresh decisions are informed.

MCF-ENV-015.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-016.objective: Ensure every reported environmental metric (energy, PUE, WUE, CUE, REF, ERF, emissions) traces to source meter data and calculation, and that restatements are controlled and disclosed, including for regulatory data-centre reporting.
MCF-ENV-016.requirement: The sustainability manager shall maintain a reporting register that links each reported metric to its calculation, source data and approver, shall retain data for the declared period, shall restate when errors exceed the declared threshold, and shall meet the content and timing of applicable regulatory reporting (for example EU Energy Efficiency Directive data-centre reporting where in scope).
MCF-ENV-016.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-017.objective: Ensure batteries in storage, transport, quarantine and end of life (UPS strings, BESS modules, rack battery backup units, spares) are inventoried, stored at safe state of charge, segregated when damaged and returned or recycled under applicable battery regulation.
MCF-ENV-017.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain an inventory of batteries held outside service, shall store lithium-ion spares at or below the declared state of charge in a designated, detected and separated location, shall quarantine damaged or swollen cells in a fire-rated container away from critical plant, and shall transfer end-of-life batteries only to authorised recyclers with documentation meeting applicable battery and waste regulation.

MCF-ENV-018.objective: Ensure refrigerants, glycols and dielectric coolants are inventoried, contained, leak-checked and handled so that toxicity, flammability (including A2L refrigerants), asphyxiation and environmental hazards are controlled for people and plant.
MCF-ENV-018.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain an inventory of refrigerant charge per system (type, mass, CO2-equivalent, ISO 817/ASHRAE 34 safety class) and of coolants and dielectric fluids, shall leak-check refrigerant systems at the frequencies required by applicable regulation, shall provide refrigerant detection, alarms and ventilation in machinery rooms and occupied spaces where concentration could exceed the practical limit, shall use only certified technicians for refrigerant work, and shall hold safety data sheets and handling procedures for every coolant.

MCF-ENV-019.objective: Ensure generator fuel and fire suppressant agents are stored, contained, transferred and disposed of safely and in compliance with permits, and that suppressant inventory reflects its environmental profile.
MCF-ENV-019.requirement: The facility operator shall store fuel in tanks with secondary containment of the declared capacity, leak detection and overfill protection, shall control deliveries with a supervised procedure, shall inspect tanks and pipework at the declared interval, and shall maintain an inventory of suppressant agents with their pressure-vessel inspection status and environmental classification, recovering agents through certified contractors.
MCF-ENV-019.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-04.

MCF-ENV-020.objective: Ensure retired AI hardware, network equipment and media are routed to reuse, refurbishment or authorised recycling with traceable records, after data sanitisation, and in line with waste electrical equipment regulation.
MCF-ENV-020.requirement: The facility operator shall route retired equipment through the decommissioning custody process (MCF-PHY-020), shall prefer reuse or refurbishment where data and security rules allow, shall transfer waste only to authorised operators with waste transfer documentation, and shall report mass by disposition route.
MCF-ENV-020.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

MCF-ENV-021.objective: Demonstrate that heat rejection, generators, transformers and battery rooms retain the capacity required by declared outcomes during extreme heat at or beyond the design ambient, and that operations has a tested response when forecasts approach design limits.
