The facility operator shall exercise the procedure before each hot season.
MCF-ENV-021.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-06, CG-05.

MCF-ENV-022.objective: Ensure long-term water availability risk is assessed for the site's water-dependent cooling, so that water stress does not become a strategic constraint on AI capability.
MCF-ENV-022.requirement: The facility owner shall assess basin-level water stress over the declared planning horizon using recognised water-risk data and climate projections, shall evaluate the security of water entitlements, and shall define the strategy (alternative sources, technology change, reduced water design) if stress exceeds the declared threshold.
MCF-ENV-022.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-03.

MCF-ENV-023.objective: Ensure that flood protection for critical plant remains adequate under projected climate change and that temporary flood defences are deployable in time.
MCF-ENV-023.requirement: The facility owner shall evaluate flood levels under the declared climate scenario and horizon, shall confirm critical plant remains above the adjusted design level plus freeboard or is protected by permanent or demountable defences, and shall maintain a flood response plan with deployment time for demountable defences shorter than the warning lead time.
MCF-ENV-023.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-09.

MCF-ENV-024.objective: Ensure long-term constraints on grid capacity, water, permits and land that could limit growth or continuation of AI capability at the site are identified, owned and fed into capacity planning.
MCF-ENV-024.requirement: The facility owner shall maintain a resource constraints register covering grid capacity availability and reinforcement timelines, water entitlement, environmental permits and their renewal dates, planning constraints and emission limits, over the declared horizon, and shall review it with capability owners when demand forecasts change.
MCF-ENV-024.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-01, CG-03.

MCF-CMP-001.objective: Establish a documented, approved accelerator architecture that links the Capability Instance's workload (training, fine-tuning, inference) to the accelerator type, memory capacity and bandwidth, scale-up domain size, scale-out fabric, power and cooling envelope, so that compute is sized and constrained by the Service Outcome rather than by procurement availability.
MCF-CMP-001.requirement: The compute engineering authority shall maintain an accelerator architecture record per cluster stating accelerator model and generation, accelerator memory capacity and bandwidth, scale-up domain size and interconnect, host CPU and memory ratio, scale-out network attachment per accelerator, per-node and per-rack power and heat, and the cooling method required. The AI platform owner shall approve the record and shall confirm its sufficiency against the performance and integrity outcomes defined for the Capability Instance.
MCF-CMP-001.unknownEffect: US3 Material: compute sufficiency for outcome unverified; CG-08 supporting evaluation

MCF-CMP-002.objective: Ensure each compute node's hardware and low-level configuration (BIOS/UEFI settings, BMC configuration, PCIe topology, NUMA and accelerator affinity, NIC attachment, power and thermal limits) matches the approved node specification, because silent configuration drift degrades performance and reliability of collective workloads.
MCF-CMP-002.requirement: The AI platform operator shall define a node configuration specification per node type and shall verify, at provisioning and at a defined interval, that every node conforms, using automated collection from the BMC (for example via Redfish) and host OS. The AI platform operator shall secure BMC interfaces with unique credentials, management-network isolation and logged access.
MCF-CMP-002.unknownEffect: US3 Material: node configuration drift possible; CG-08 supporting

MCF-CMP-003.objective: Ensure rack-scale systems (integrated compute trays, scale-up switch trays, power shelves, busbars, liquid manifolds) are composed, connected and accepted as a unit, with their facility interfaces (power, liquid, network, weight) verified against the facility design.
MCF-CMP-003.requirement: The AI platform operator shall maintain a rack-scale composition record for each rack type (trays, switch trays, power shelves, manifold and QD layout, cable/backplane mapping) and shall verify each installed rack at acceptance. The facility operator and AI platform operator shall jointly sign the facility interface checklist covering power feeds, liquid connections and flow, floor loading and network uplinks before energisation.
MCF-CMP-003.unknownEffect: US3 Material: facility interface conformance uncertain; CG-06 and CG-05 supporting

MCF-CMP-004.objective: Maintain a single, approved, version-controlled compute baseline (hardware bill of materials, firmware set, driver and runtime stack, OS image, configuration) against which every node can be reconciled and every change can be measured.
MCF-CMP-004.requirement: The AI platform operator shall publish an approved compute baseline per node type that enumerates hardware components, firmware versions, driver and runtime versions, OS image hash and configuration profile, shall approve changes to it under change control, and shall reconcile the deployed fleet to it continuously, reporting the fraction of nodes on the current baseline.
MCF-CMP-004.unknownEffect: US3 Material: as-built state uncertain; CG-02 supporting

MCF-CMP-005.objective: Document the cluster topology (nodes, scale-up domains, scale-out rails, storage attachment, management plane) so that job placement, failure analysis and capacity statements can be reasoned about against physical and logical locality.
MCF-CMP-005.requirement: The AI platform operator shall maintain a machine-readable cluster topology describing node-to-scale-up-domain membership, node-to-rail and leaf mapping, rack, power and cooling domain of every node, and storage and management attachment. The compute engineering authority shall reconcile the topology with the fabric (NET-01) and facility models at each change.
MCF-CMP-005.unknownEffect: US3 Material: placement and failure analysis uncertain; CG-02 supporting

MCF-CMP-006.objective: Ensure each scale-up domain (the accelerator group joined by the high-bandwidth, low-latency interconnect, from a single node to a rack-scale domain) delivers its rated bandwidth with all links and switches healthy, and that a degraded domain is detected and withdrawn before it slows or corrupts a training job.
MCF-CMP-006.requirement: The AI platform operator shall validate every scale-up domain at acceptance and at a defined interval by running an all-to-all or all-reduce bandwidth test against the platform's rated performance, shall monitor interconnect link errors, retrains and lane degradation continuously, and shall automatically drain domains that fall below the declared bandwidth threshold or exceed the link-error threshold.
MCF-CMP-006.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN for training outcomes relying on unvalidated scale-up domains

MCF-CMP-007.objective: Ensure logical partitions of the cluster (tenant, project, production versus test, accelerator partitioning such as multi-instance modes) are enforced so that one partition's jobs, faults or administrators cannot consume, disrupt or read another's resources.
MCF-CMP-007.requirement: The AI platform operator shall define partitions with membership, quotas, network and storage isolation, and administrator scope, shall enforce them in the scheduler, fabric and storage configuration, and shall verify enforcement after each change. Where accelerator-level partitioning is used, the AI platform operator shall document its isolation properties as stated by the OEM.
MCF-CMP-007.unknownEffect: US3 Material: isolation uncertain; CG-09 and CG-15 supporting

MCF-CMP-008.objective: Ensure the cluster is laid out so that loss of any single facility or infrastructure fault domain (rack, power feed group, CDU loop, leaf switch, scale-up domain) removes no more than the declared fraction of capacity and does not halt the Service Outcome beyond tolerance.
MCF-CMP-008.requirement: The compute engineering authority shall map each compute node to its facility and infrastructure fault domains, shall limit the fraction of a Capability Instance's capacity in any single fault domain to the declared maximum, and shall demonstrate, by controlled drain or real event, that loss of a representative fault domain is contained and that jobs resume on remaining capacity within the recovery tolerance.
MCF-CMP-008.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-09 UNKNOWN for compute containment

MCF-CMP-009.objective: Measure the accelerator capacity actually usable by the Capability Instance (healthy, schedulable, at rated performance, not thermally or power-throttled) and compare it with the capacity the outcome requires, rather than reporting installed accelerator count.
MCF-CMP-009.requirement: The AI platform operator shall compute and report, at least daily, usable accelerator capacity as installed accelerators minus those drained, failed, quarantined, under repair, reserved, or throttled below the declared performance threshold, and shall compare it with the outcome's required capacity. The AI platform owner shall be notified when usable capacity falls below the required level.
MCF-CMP-009.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN for capacity-dependent outcomes

MCF-CMP-010.objective: Ensure the workload scheduler (for example Slurm or Kubernetes-based schedulers) enforces placement, priority, quota, topology-awareness and health-gating so that jobs land only on healthy nodes in the right topology and privileged scheduler functions are restricted.
MCF-CMP-010.requirement: The AI platform operator shall configure the scheduler to admit jobs only to nodes passing health checks, to apply topology-aware placement for scale-up and rail locality, to enforce quotas and priorities per partition, and shall restrict scheduler administrative actions (drain, reservation, priority override) to authorised roles with logging. The scheduler control plane shall have documented high availability.
MCF-CMP-010.unknownEffect: US3 Material: job placement integrity uncertain; CG-08 supporting

MCF-CMP-011.objective: Ensure capacity required for priority outcomes, hot spares and recovery (re-running from checkpoint after failure) is reserved and actually available when needed, rather than consumed by lower-priority work.
MCF-CMP-011.requirement: The AI platform operator shall reserve accelerator capacity for declared priority outcomes and for recovery (hot spare nodes or scale-up domains), shall verify daily that reservations are intact and healthy, and shall be able to reclaim reserved capacity from lower-priority jobs within the declared time.
MCF-CMP-011.unknownEffect: US3 Material: recovery capacity uncertain; CG-10 supporting

MCF-CMP-012.objective: Detect and manage contention for shared resources (accelerators, fabric, storage bandwidth, power caps) so that one workload's demand does not degrade another priority outcome beyond tolerance, including coordinated facility power capping.
MCF-CMP-012.requirement: The AI platform operator shall define contention policies (preemption, fair share, bandwidth QoS, power-cap allocation), shall monitor indicators of contention (queue wait, job slowdown, fabric and storage saturation), and shall act when priority outcomes degrade beyond tolerance. Where facility-driven power capping is used, the AI platform operator and facility operator shall agree the capping protocol and its effect on priority outcomes.
MCF-CMP-012.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: confidence ceiling CONF-2 for performance outcomes

MCF-CMP-013.objective: Ensure firmware on accelerators, NICs, BMCs, BIOS/UEFI, interconnect switches and power shelves is at approved, authenticated versions across the fleet, because firmware mismatch is a common-mode source of hangs, errors and security exposure.
MCF-CMP-013.requirement: The AI platform operator shall maintain an approved firmware matrix per node and rack type, shall verify signature or provenance of each firmware image before deployment, shall measure firmware versions across the fleet automatically, and shall remediate drift within the declared time. Where the platform supports it, the AI platform operator shall use device attestation (for example SPDM measurements or TPM-based measured boot) to confirm firmware identity.
MCF-CMP-013.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN where fleet firmware state is unverified

MCF-CMP-014.objective: Ensure accelerator drivers, communication libraries, runtimes, kernel and container base images form a tested compatible stack, and that workloads run only on stacks in the compatibility matrix.
MCF-CMP-014.requirement: The AI platform operator shall maintain a compatibility matrix linking firmware, kernel, accelerator driver, communication library, runtime and container base images, shall test each matrix entry before approval, and shall prevent workloads from running on unapproved combinations through image and node labelling.
MCF-CMP-014.unknownEffect: US3 Material: stack compatibility uncertain; CG-08 supporting

MCF-CMP-015.objective: Ensure firmware, driver and software upgrades are tested on representative workloads and rolled out in stages with soak periods and automatic halt criteria, so that a defective release cannot become a fleet-wide common-mode failure.
MCF-CMP-015.requirement: The AI platform operator shall test each upgrade on a staging environment with representative workloads (including multi-node collective tests and checkpoint/restore), shall roll out in stages starting with a canary cohort spread across fault domains, shall define soak periods and halt criteria based on error rates and performance, and shall record each stage's go/no-go decision.
MCF-CMP-015.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-14 UNKNOWN for compute change control

MCF-CMP-016.objective: Ensure every firmware and software change can be rolled back to the previous known-good baseline within the declared time, including components where rollback is constrained (anti-rollback fuses, one-way firmware migrations).
MCF-CMP-016.requirement: The AI platform operator shall define a rollback procedure for each change class, shall identify components where rollback is constrained or impossible and treat them as higher-risk changes, shall retain previous known-good images, and shall test rollback in staging for each change before production rollout.
MCF-CMP-016.unknownEffect: US3 Material: recovery from defective change uncertain; CG-10 supporting

MCF-CMP-017.objective: Collect accelerator telemetry (temperature, power, clocks, throttle reasons, memory ECC counts, page/row retirement, interconnect errors, utilisation) at sufficient frequency and completeness to detect degradation and to correlate compute behaviour with facility events.
MCF-CMP-017.requirement: The AI platform operator shall collect accelerator telemetry from every in-scope accelerator at the declared interval using vendor management interfaces, shall monitor collection completeness, shall time-synchronise telemetry with facility (BMS/EPMS) data, and shall retain it for the declared period.
MCF-CMP-017.unknownEffect: US3 Material: degradation detection and thermal correlation limited; CG-08 and CG-06 supporting

MCF-CMP-018.objective: Ensure each node's health is checked before, during and after jobs by automated checks (accelerator diagnostics, memory, interconnect, NIC, storage mount, thermal state) and unhealthy nodes are drained before they cause job failure.
MCF-CMP-018.requirement: The AI platform operator shall run automated health checks at job prolog/epilog and at a periodic interval, shall define pass criteria per check, shall drain nodes failing a check automatically, and shall track drained nodes to repair or return-to-service.
MCF-CMP-018.unknownEffect: US3 Material: job reliability uncertain; CG-08 supporting

MCF-CMP-019.objective: Detect accelerator and node errors that threaten job integrity (uncorrectable ECC, rising correctable ECC, memory row remapping exhaustion, vendor fatal error events such as XID-type events, PCIe AER errors, interconnect CRC errors) and silent data corruption, and respond before corrupted results propagate into checkpoints or models.
MCF-CMP-019.requirement: The AI platform operator shall classify accelerator and node error events by severity with defined automatic actions (drain, reset, RMA), shall trend correctable error rates against thresholds, and shall run periodic silent-data-corruption screening (known-answer tests) across the fleet. The AI platform operator shall link detected corruption to affected jobs and checkpoints for integrity assessment.
MCF-CMP-019.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN for integrity outcomes

MCF-CMP-020.objective: Maintain performance baselines (single-accelerator throughput, scale-up bandwidth, multi-node collective bandwidth, representative training step time) so that degradation from hardware, firmware, thermal or fabric causes is detected quantitatively.
MCF-CMP-020.requirement: The AI platform operator shall define baseline benchmarks per node type and cluster scale, shall run them at acceptance, after changes and at a periodic interval, and shall investigate deviations beyond the declared threshold.
MCF-CMP-020.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: confidence ceiling CONF-2 for performance outcomes

MCF-CMP-021.objective: Ensure new and repaired hardware enters service only after verified identity, baseline conformance and burn-in acceptance, so that infant-mortality failures and counterfeit or mis-configured components are caught before production.
MCF-CMP-021.requirement: The AI platform operator shall provision nodes through an automated pipeline that verifies component identity against the purchase and provenance records, applies the approved baseline, runs a burn-in and acceptance suite (stress, memory, interconnect, thermal, storage) for the declared duration, and records acceptance before the node becomes schedulable.
MCF-CMP-021.unknownEffect: US3 Material: infant-mortality risk; CG-08 supporting

MCF-CMP-022.objective: Ensure spare accelerators, nodes, trays, switch trays, NICs and cables are held in quantities and locations sufficient to restore usable capacity within tolerance, and that RMA turnaround is tracked against supplier obligations.
MCF-CMP-022.requirement: The AI platform operator shall size spares from observed failure rates and lead times, shall hold spares on site or within the declared logistics time, shall track RMA turnaround against contractual obligations, and shall ensure returned parts are sanitised or tracked under custody.
MCF-CMP-022.unknownEffect: US3 Material: restoration capacity uncertain; CG-10 supporting

MCF-CMP-023.objective: Ensure nodes and scale-up domains can be rebuilt from bare metal to an accepted, schedulable state within the declared time after failure, corruption or mass events (for example after a power or cooling outage), including re-qualification before rejoining production.
MCF-CMP-023.requirement: The AI platform operator shall maintain an automated rebuild path (image, baseline, configuration, credentials, health and bandwidth re-qualification) that does not depend on services lost in the same event, shall define the rebuild time objective per node and for a mass rebuild of a declared fraction of the cluster, and shall exercise mass rebuild at a defined interval. After facility power or cooling events, the AI platform operator shall re-qualify affected nodes before readmission.
MCF-CMP-023.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-10 UNKNOWN for compute recovery

MCF-CMP-024.objective: Ensure retired or returned compute hardware (nodes, accelerators with memory, BMCs, boot drives, NICs with persistent configuration) is removed from inventory, sanitised, and disposed of with custody, so that data, credentials and model weights are not exposed and the asset register stays accurate.
MCF-CMP-024.requirement: The AI platform operator shall execute a retirement procedure that revokes credentials and attestation identities, sanitises persistent storage per a recognised sanitisation standard with verification, resets BMC and firmware secrets, updates the asset register and topology, and records custody to disposal or resale.
MCF-CMP-024.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: no gate; record for data-protection and inventory assertions

MCF-STO-001.objective: Ensure the storage tier holding training and fine-tuning datasets is designed for the read pattern of data loaders at cluster scale, preserves dataset versions and lineage, and keeps data within declared sovereignty and residency boundaries.
MCF-STO-001.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall document the training data tier (system type, for example parallel file system or object store with cache; capacity; read throughput per accelerator; dataset versioning and lineage mechanism; locations and jurisdictions of every copy). The data owner shall approve the residency and sovereignty constraints and shall confirm that every copy, cache and replica lies within them.
MCF-STO-001.unknownEffect: US3 Material: data-tier adequacy or residency uncertain; CG-08 supporting; residency gaps reported to the decision as condition

MCF-STO-002.objective: Ensure the checkpoint tier is sized so that model and optimiser state can be written within the declared checkpoint window at the declared interval, with the interval chosen against observed failure rates, and that checkpoints are placed in a fault domain independent of the compute they protect.
MCF-STO-002.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall document checkpoint size per job class, required write bandwidth (checkpoint size ÷ checkpoint window), checkpoint interval and its derivation from job-level failure rate and checkpoint cost, retention count, and the fault-domain separation between the checkpoint tier and the protected compute. The AI platform operator shall confirm the parameters per production job class.
MCF-STO-002.unknownEffect: US3 Material: checkpoint adequacy uncertain; CG-10 and CG-08 supporting

MCF-STO-003.objective: Ensure trained models, adapters, tokenisers, configurations and release artefacts are stored in a versioned, access-controlled, integrity-protected registry from which deployments and recoveries draw known-good, hash-verified artefacts.
MCF-STO-003.requirement: The AI platform operator shall store model and release artefacts in a registry that assigns immutable versions, records content hashes and provenance (training run, dataset version, checkpoint), restricts write and delete to authorised roles, and verifies hashes at deployment. The storage service owner shall protect the registry under MCF-STO-013 to MCF-STO-016.
MCF-STO-003.unknownEffect: US3 Material: artefact integrity uncertain; CG-10 supporting

MCF-STO-004.objective: Ensure long-term retention of datasets, model versions and checkpoints needed for reproducibility, audit or regulatory purposes is held on a durable archive tier with defined retention, retrievability, integrity checking and media-refresh plans.
MCF-STO-004.requirement: The storage service owner shall define retention classes for archived AI data, shall store archives with fixity checks and at least the declared number of geographically or administratively separate copies, shall test retrieval at a defined interval, and shall plan media or format migration before end of support.
MCF-STO-004.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: long-term reproducibility confidence capped

MCF-STO-005.objective: Demonstrate that the storage system delivers the aggregate read throughput for data loading and the aggregate write throughput for checkpointing that the outcome requires, at full cluster concurrency and in degraded states (failed server, rebuild in progress).
MCF-STO-005.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall demonstrate, by benchmark at acceptance and after material change, that aggregate read and write throughput and IOPS meet the required values at the declared client concurrency, including with one storage server or enclosure failed and during erasure-coding or RAID rebuild. The AI platform operator shall measure production checkpoint write times and compare them with the window in MCF-STO-002.
MCF-STO-005.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN for training outcomes

MCF-STO-006.objective: Ensure metadata operations (open, create, stat, list) scale to the concurrency of AI jobs, because many-small-file datasets and synchronous checkpoint creation can saturate metadata services and stall entire clusters.
MCF-STO-006.requirement: The storage service owner shall define required metadata operation rates and latency at peak concurrency, shall monitor metadata latency and queue depth continuously, and shall apply workload guidance (file packing, sharded checkpoints, directory fan-out limits) agreed with the AI platform operator.
MCF-STO-006.unknownEffect: US3 Material: metadata-induced stalls possible; CG-08 supporting

MCF-STO-007.objective: Maintain free capacity above the level at which the storage system's performance, rebuild ability or checkpoint retention degrade, so that capacity exhaustion never halts checkpointing.
MCF-STO-007.requirement: The storage service owner shall define a capacity headroom threshold per tier that accounts for performance degradation at high fill, rebuild space and retention of N checkpoints, shall alert at warning and critical thresholds, and shall enforce quotas so that one job or tenant cannot exhaust a shared tier.
MCF-STO-007.unknownEffect: US3 Material: exhaustion risk; CG-08 supporting

MCF-STO-008.objective: Ensure the storage system absorbs synchronised write bursts (many ranks checkpointing simultaneously, several jobs checkpointing at once, restart storms after an outage) without timeouts, job failure or degradation of other tenants.
MCF-STO-008.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall characterise peak burst demand (concurrent checkpoints, restart read storm), shall provide burst absorption (client-side or burst-buffer tier, QoS, admission control or staggered checkpoint scheduling), and shall demonstrate by test or production evidence that the declared burst completes within the window without client timeouts or impact beyond tolerance on other workloads.
MCF-STO-008.unknownEffect: US3 Material: burst resilience uncertain; CG-08 and CG-09 supporting

MCF-STO-009.objective: Ensure data, checkpoints and model artefacts are protected end-to-end against undetected corruption from client to media and back, so that silent corruption cannot enter training or deployment.
MCF-STO-009.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall implement end-to-end integrity protection (application or file-level checksums on checkpoints and artefacts, plus storage-level checksums or protection information) and shall verify checksums on read and on restore. The AI platform operator shall verify checkpoint checksums before resuming training from them and shall treat a verification failure as an integrity incident.
MCF-STO-009.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN for integrity outcomes

MCF-STO-010.objective: Ensure file-system or object-store metadata (namespace, layout, allocation, object maps) is protected, consistent and recoverable, because metadata loss can render intact data unreachable for the whole tier.
MCF-STO-010.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall protect metadata with redundancy independent of the data path (replicated metadata servers or volumes), shall run consistency checks at a defined interval, shall back up metadata where the platform supports it, and shall demonstrate metadata service failover and recovery on a test system or in a controlled test.
MCF-STO-010.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN for storage function

MCF-STO-011.objective: Detect latent media and data errors before they are needed by scrubbing stored data and verifying checksums on a schedule that completes within the declared cycle.
MCF-STO-011.requirement: The storage service owner shall schedule scrubbing so that all data on in-scope tiers is verified within the declared cycle, shall monitor scrub completion and error rates, and shall repair detected errors from redundancy promptly.
MCF-STO-011.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: confidence ceiling CONF-2 for integrity operating claims

MCF-STO-012.objective: Ensure storage configuration (protection schemes, quotas, exports, client mount options, QoS, replication policies, retention locks) matches the approved baseline across all storage systems and clients.
MCF-STO-012.requirement: The storage service owner shall maintain an approved storage configuration baseline, shall detect drift automatically, shall apply changes under change control with post-change verification, and shall verify client mount options and versions across the fleet.
MCF-STO-012.unknownEffect: US3 Material: protection settings may differ from design; CG-14 supporting

MCF-STO-013.objective: Ensure snapshots of datasets, artefact registries and checkpoint directories are taken at the declared frequency, retained, protected from deletion by ordinary users, and actually restorable, to recover from accidental deletion or logical corruption.
MCF-STO-013.requirement: The storage service owner shall configure snapshot schedules and retention per protected namespace, shall restrict snapshot deletion to authorised roles, shall monitor snapshot success, and shall restore from snapshot on a sample basis at a defined interval.
MCF-STO-013.unknownEffect: US3 Material: logical recovery uncertain; CG-10 supporting

MCF-STO-014.objective: Ensure data required for recovery is replicated to a target in an independent fault domain (another hall, site or region) within the declared recovery point objective, within permitted jurisdictions, and that replication lag and failures are detected.
MCF-STO-014.requirement: The storage service owner shall define replication scope, target, mode (synchronous or asynchronous) and RPO per data class, shall place targets outside the source's power, cooling, network and administrative fault domains as declared, shall keep targets within permitted jurisdictions, shall monitor lag, and shall demonstrate failover or restore from the replica.
MCF-STO-014.unknownEffect: US3 Material: off-domain recovery uncertain; CG-10 supporting

MCF-STO-015.objective: Ensure erasure coding or RAID protection is configured so that stripes span independent failure domains (drive, server, enclosure, rack) and tolerate the declared number of concurrent failures, with rebuild completing before a further failure is likely.
MCF-STO-015.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall document the protection scheme per tier (for example k+m), the failure domains across which stripes are placed, the number of concurrent domain failures tolerated, and expected rebuild time at current capacity; shall verify placement against physical topology; and shall demonstrate rebuild of a failed component within the declared time.
MCF-STO-015.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-09 UNKNOWN for storage containment

MCF-STO-016.objective: Ensure at least one copy of recovery-critical data (latest good checkpoints, model artefacts, key datasets, storage and platform configuration) is immutable for its retention period and held in a separate administrative and fault domain, so that ransomware, privileged-account compromise or operator error cannot destroy every copy.
MCF-STO-016.requirement: The storage service owner shall maintain an immutable recovery copy of declared recovery-critical data with retention locks that cannot be shortened by administrators of the primary system, in a separate administrative domain with separate credentials, and shall demonstrate restore from it within the declared time.
MCF-STO-016.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-10 UNKNOWN for recovery from destructive events

MCF-STO-017.objective: Ensure each checkpoint is complete, consistent across all shards and ranks, durably committed and verifiable before it is marked good and before older checkpoints are deleted.
MCF-STO-017.requirement: The AI platform operator shall mark a checkpoint good only after all shards are written, flushed to durable storage, checksummed and manifest-recorded; shall never delete the previous good checkpoint until the new one is verified; and shall retain the declared number of good checkpoints. The storage service owner shall ensure the checkpoint tier honours flush semantics.
MCF-STO-017.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN for training integrity

MCF-STO-018.objective: Ensure a training or fine-tuning job can be restarted from its latest good checkpoint on available capacity (including a different set of nodes or a reduced node count where the framework supports re-sharding) within the declared restart time objective.
MCF-STO-018.requirement: The AI platform operator shall maintain restart procedures and automation for production job classes, shall verify that checkpoints can be loaded on a different node set, shall measure time from failure to resumed training, and shall exercise restart at a defined interval including after a storage or facility event.
MCF-STO-018.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-10 UNKNOWN for training recovery

MCF-STO-019.objective: Ensure that after a site, power or cooling event, storage services are brought back in a defined order (power and cooling verified, network and time, identity, metadata services, data servers, consistency checks, client mounts, then job readmission) so that recovery does not corrupt data or stall on hidden dependencies.
MCF-STO-019.requirement: The storage service owner shall maintain a storage recovery sequence with prerequisites, hold points and verification checks for each step, aligned with facility (THM/POW) and compute (CMP) recovery, and shall exercise it at a defined interval.
MCF-STO-019.unknownEffect: US3 Material: recovery order uncertain; CG-10 supporting

MCF-STO-020.objective: Demonstrate by periodic restore tests that every protected data class can be restored from each protection mechanism (snapshot, replica, immutable copy) to a usable, integrity-verified state within the declared recovery time, and that restored checkpoints actually resume training.
MCF-STO-020.requirement: The storage service owner shall run restore tests at a defined interval for each protected data class and protection mechanism, shall verify integrity of restored data by checksum, and, for checkpoints, the AI platform operator shall resume a training job from the restored checkpoint and confirm loss and step continuity.
MCF-STO-020.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-10 UNKNOWN for data recovery

MCF-STO-021.objective: Collect storage telemetry (throughput, IOPS, latency percentiles, metadata latency, capacity, rebuild state, client errors, replication lag) with completeness monitoring and time synchronisation, to detect degradation and support incident analysis.
MCF-STO-021.requirement: The storage service owner shall collect telemetry from all in-scope storage systems and a representative sample of clients at the declared interval, shall monitor collection completeness, shall time-synchronise with compute and facility telemetry, and shall alert on thresholds.

MCF-STO-022.objective: Forecast storage capacity and performance demand from planned training runs, dataset growth, checkpoint retention and model registry growth, against procurement lead times, so that expansion arrives before headroom thresholds are reached.
MCF-STO-022.requirement: The storage service owner shall forecast capacity and throughput demand over a horizon at least as long as procurement and deployment lead time, using the AI platform's planned workloads, and shall trigger expansion when the forecast crosses headroom thresholds within the lead time.

MCF-STO-023.objective: Monitor drive and media health (SMART/NVMe health logs, wear level, media errors, annualised failure rate by model and lot) and replace degrading media proactively before redundancy is consumed.
MCF-STO-023.requirement: The storage service owner shall collect media health indicators, shall define proactive replacement thresholds, shall track failure rates by model and lot, and shall replace media before failure where thresholds are crossed.

MCF-STO-024.objective: Ensure storage media and systems leaving service, RMA or tenant reassignment are sanitised to a recognised standard with verification, so that training data, model weights and credentials cannot be recovered.
MCF-STO-024.requirement: The storage service owner shall sanitise media by clear, purge or destroy methods appropriate to media type and data classification under a recognised sanitisation standard, shall verify sanitisation, shall issue per-device certificates, and shall keep custody until sanitisation or destruction is complete, including for media sent for RMA.
MCF-STO-024.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: no gate; record for data-protection assertions

MCF-NET-001.objective: Ensure the scale-up and scale-out fabrics are built to an approved topology whose bisection bandwidth, tiering, rail assignment and endpoint attachment match what the declared training and inference Service Outcomes require.
MCF-NET-001.requirement: The network architecture owner shall maintain an approved topology design for every back-end (scale-out) fabric and scale-up domain in scope, stating the topology class (for example rail-optimised multi-plane, two-tier leaf-spine or three-tier fat-tree/Clos, or rack-scale scale-up domain), switch radix, tier count, rail and plane assignment, endpoint-to-leaf mapping and the design bisection bandwidth per Capability Instance. The fabric operations lead shall reconcile the as-built fabric (LLDP or subnet-manager discovered topology, cabling records and port maps) to the approved design at commissioning and after every material change, and shall record every deviation as either an approved variance or a Finding.
MCF-NET-001.unknownEffect: US4: CG-08 cannot PASS while as-built topology of a gate-critical fabric is unreconciled; record UNKNOWN U5 or U3 as applicable.

MCF-NET-002.objective: Ensure that logical redundancy in fabrics, inter-hall links and WAN/DCI connections is matched by physically diverse paths, so a single cable route, conduit, carrier or building entry cannot defeat redundant connectivity.
MCF-NET-002.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define, for each redundant path group (spine uplinks between halls, storage and front-end uplinks, WAN and data-centre interconnect circuits, OOB uplinks), the required diversity attributes: separate cable routes and containment, separate building entries, separate carriers or carrier-neutral dark-fibre routes, and separate optical line systems where DWDM is used. The connectivity manager shall obtain route evidence (carrier KMZ or route maps, cable-route surveys, containment records) for each path and shall record every shared segment, shared conduit, shared meet-me room or shared upstream carrier as a common-mode dependency.
MCF-NET-002.unknownEffect: US3 by default; US4 against CG-03 where the undisclosed segment carries the only DCI path for a gate-critical outcome.

MCF-NET-003.objective: Ensure each fabric tier's oversubscription ratio is a deliberate design decision justified against the expected traffic matrix of the declared workloads, so collective and storage traffic are not throttled by uplink scarcity.
MCF-NET-003.requirement: The network architecture owner shall state the design oversubscription ratio at every tier boundary (leaf-to-spine, spine-to-superspine, pod-to-core, storage and front-end uplinks) and shall justify each ratio against the traffic matrix of the declared workloads, including all-reduce, all-to-all (for example expert-parallel) and checkpoint bursts. The fabric operations lead shall re-derive effective oversubscription after link failures, partial builds and planned maintenance, and shall record the minimum tolerated effective ratio for each Service Outcome.
MCF-NET-003.unknownEffect: US3: unjustified ratios cap performance assurance; CG-08 SUPPORTING evaluation required.

MCF-NET-004.objective: Ensure fabric failure domains (switch, rail, plane, pod, spine group, subnet manager, controller, power feed and cooling zone) are designed so that any single credible failure stays within a blast radius the Service Outcome tolerates.
MCF-NET-004.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define the fault domains of each fabric, including each switch, rail, plane, pod, spine group, subnet manager or fabric controller instance, and the power and cooling zones serving fabric equipment, and shall state for each the maximum affected endpoints and the resulting outcome impact. The fabric operations lead shall demonstrate, by controlled test or by analysed incident, that loss of a leaf, a spine, a rail or plane, a subnet-manager master and one power feed to a switch row each stay within the declared blast radius, and that fabric equipment does not share an undisclosed power or cooling fault domain with its own redundancy.
MCF-NET-004.unknownEffect: US4: CG-09 cannot PASS while a gate-critical fabric's single-failure blast radius is untested and unanalysed.

MCF-NET-005.objective: Ensure the fabric has a measured latency baseline (idle and loaded, per path class) against which degradation can be detected and Service Outcome performance claims tested.
MCF-NET-005.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall establish and maintain latency baselines for each path class (intra-leaf, intra-pod, cross-spine, cross-plane, storage path, front-end path) including idle round-trip time, loaded tail latency at defined percentiles and switch-hop count, measured with a repeatable method (for example perftest-class RDMA latency tools or active probing). The fabric operations lead shall alert on deviation from baseline beyond a defined threshold and shall re-baseline after any material NOS, firmware, topology or congestion-control change.
MCF-NET-005.unknownEffect: US2: absent baselines reduce confidence in performance claims; US3 if a performance Service Outcome depends on latency tolerance.

MCF-NET-006.objective: Ensure packet loss, link errors and transport retransmissions are monitored against thresholds so that degrading links, optics and lossless-class failures are detected before they defeat job progress.
MCF-NET-006.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall monitor, per port and per traffic class, pre-FEC and post-FEC bit error indicators, FEC corrected and uncorrectable codeword counts, CRC/symbol errors, link flaps, discards, and RDMA transport retransmission and out-of-sequence counters at NICs, against defined thresholds. The fabric operations lead shall automatically isolate or drain links that exceed uncorrectable-error or flap thresholds, shall track each to closure, and shall verify that the lossless traffic class shows no congestion drops under normal operation.
MCF-NET-006.unknownEffect: US3: unmonitored error classes may hide job-defeating link faults; CG-08 SUPPORTING evaluation.

MCF-NET-007.objective: Ensure congestion control and lossless configuration (ECN marking, PFC, DCQCN-style or vendor rate control, adaptive routing, InfiniBand credit-based flow control) keep fabrics stable under incast and many-to-one load, and that lossless-mode hazards such as PFC storms and deadlocks are prevented or contained.
MCF-NET-007.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define a congestion-control design per fabric stating traffic-class mapping, ECN marking thresholds, PFC enablement and headroom per priority, PFC watchdog behaviour, end-host rate-control algorithm and parameters, and adaptive routing settings, and shall analyse the design for cyclic buffer dependency (PFC deadlock) and pause-storm propagation. The fabric operations lead shall verify by controlled test that incast and congestion scenarios representative of declared workloads do not cause lossless-class drops, sustained pause propagation beyond the congested port, or deadlock, and that the PFC watchdog detects and breaks a stuck-pause condition within the configured time.
MCF-NET-007.unknownEffect: US4: CG-08 cannot PASS for an RDMA-over-Ethernet fabric while lossless behaviour under congestion is untested.

MCF-NET-008.objective: Ensure collective operations (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, all-to-all) achieve the bus bandwidth and step-time required by declared training and inference outcomes at full and degraded scale.
MCF-NET-008.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall run a defined collective benchmark suite (for example NCCL- or RCCL-class tests and a representative workload proxy) at commissioning, after every material fabric, NIC or library change and at a defined periodic interval, covering message sizes and scales used by declared workloads, and shall compare achieved bus bandwidth and latency to acceptance targets. The capability owner shall set the acceptance targets from the performance Service Outcome and shall accept or reject results for degraded scale (for example one plane or one spine unavailable).
MCF-NET-008.unknownEffect: US4: CG-08 cannot PASS while collective performance at required scale is unmeasured.

MCF-NET-009.objective: Ensure the storage network (dedicated or converged) delivers the throughput, latency and isolation needed for dataset reads and checkpoint write bursts without interfering with collective traffic.
MCF-NET-009.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define the storage network design: whether storage traffic uses a dedicated fabric, a dedicated plane or a separate traffic class on the compute fabric; the path from compute nodes to storage servers and metadata services; capacity per storage server; and the traffic-class and congestion policy that prevents checkpoint bursts from degrading collective traffic. The storage platform owner and fabric operations lead shall jointly test a synchronised checkpoint write and a dataset-read burst at declared scale and confirm achieved throughput and the effect on concurrent collective performance meet targets.
MCF-NET-009.unknownEffect: US4: CG-08 cannot PASS while checkpoint-path throughput at declared scale is unverified (scenario X06).

MCF-NET-010.objective: Ensure the front-end network that carries user, API, inference request, orchestration and data-ingest traffic is built to an approved, redundant design and reconciles to it.
MCF-NET-010.requirement: The network architecture owner shall maintain an approved front-end network design covering node attachment (dual-homed or single-homed), routing protocol and ECMP design, uplinks to core and edge, load-balancer and gateway placement, and capacity for inference request and data-ingest peaks. The network operations manager shall reconcile as-built configuration and attachment to the design at commissioning and after material changes, and shall confirm that loss of a single front-end switch or uplink does not disconnect inference endpoints or orchestration control traffic beyond tolerance.
MCF-NET-010.unknownEffect: US3: unreconciled front-end attachment may hide single points of failure for inference outcomes.

MCF-NET-011.objective: Ensure gateways, load balancers, NAT, firewalls and edge routers on the service path operate within capacity, with health monitoring and redundancy that sustain inference and data-ingest outcomes.
MCF-NET-011.requirement: The network operations manager shall operate each service gateway cluster (load balancers, inference API gateways, NAT, edge routers and in-path firewalls) as a redundant pair or cluster with health checks, session-state handling and capacity monitoring, and shall define capacity thresholds for connections, throughput and TLS handshakes. The network operations manager shall review gateway capacity and failover events monthly and shall demonstrate that gateway failover occurred, or was tested, within tolerance in the assessment period.
MCF-NET-011.unknownEffect: US3: unknown gateway capacity or failover behaviour conditions the inference availability claim.

MCF-NET-012.objective: Ensure tenant, workload and traffic-class isolation on shared fabrics prevents one tenant or job from degrading, observing or reaching another beyond tolerance.
MCF-NET-012.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define the isolation model for shared fabrics: InfiniBand partition keys, VRFs, VXLAN/EVPN segments, VLANs, RDMA queue-pair and memory-region protections, traffic-class guarantees and rate limits. The fabric operations lead shall verify by test that endpoints in one isolation domain cannot reach endpoints in another, and that a saturating or misbehaving tenant cannot reduce another tenant's guaranteed bandwidth or trigger fabric-wide pause beyond the defined tolerance.
MCF-NET-012.unknownEffect: US3 for single-tenant estates; US4 against CG-09 for multi-tenant platforms where isolation is a declared outcome.

MCF-NET-013.objective: Ensure management traffic for switches, servers, BMCs, PDUs, storage and facility gateways traverses a management network separated from data and tenant networks, so data-plane failure or compromise does not remove management reach.
MCF-NET-013.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define the management network architecture, separating in-band management, BMC/out-of-band management and facility OT management, and shall prohibit management interfaces from being reachable from tenant or data networks except through defined conduits. The network operations manager shall reconcile the management network attachment of every switch management port, BMC, PDU, console server and storage controller to the design, and shall record any device whose management is only reachable in-band as a Finding.
MCF-NET-013.unknownEffect: US3; escalates to US4 against CG-15 where BMCs or facility gateways are reachable from tenant networks.

MCF-NET-014.objective: Ensure serial console and remote KVM access to network, compute and storage devices exists, is authenticated and is reachable independently of the data plane.
MCF-NET-014.requirement: The network operations manager shall provide serial console access to every switch, router, firewall and storage controller, and BMC/KVM access to every server, through console servers or OOB infrastructure that is independent of the data fabric, and shall require individual authentication, session logging and role-based authorisation for console sessions. The network operations manager shall verify console reachability for every device at a defined interval and after rack moves.
MCF-NET-014.unknownEffect: US3: unknown console reach weakens recovery assurance; SUPPORTING evaluation for CG-10.

MCF-NET-015.objective: Ensure the out-of-band management network remains available when the data fabric, site core, primary identity services or primary WAN fail, so restoration can proceed.
MCF-NET-015.requirement: The network architecture owner shall design the OOB network with its own switching, power supply from a protected source with defined autonomy, independent upstream connectivity (for example a separate carrier or cellular path), and locally available authentication and name resolution, and shall document every dependency the OOB network has on the systems it is used to recover. The network operations manager shall test at a defined interval that OOB access to critical devices is achievable with the production fabric, primary WAN and primary identity provider unavailable.
MCF-NET-015.unknownEffect: US4: CG-10 cannot PASS while OOB independence from the systems it recovers is unverified.

MCF-NET-016.objective: Ensure emergency access to network devices and controllers works when central authentication is unavailable, and that its use is controlled, logged and reviewed.
MCF-NET-016.requirement: The network operations manager shall provision break-glass local credentials or offline authentication for network devices, fabric controllers, subnet managers and console servers, stored in a sealed or vaulted mechanism with dual control, and shall test break-glass login on a sample of device classes at a defined interval. The infrastructure security owner shall review every break-glass use within a defined time, rotate the credentials afterwards, and confirm that break-glass accounts are disabled for routine use.
MCF-NET-016.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 if no tested emergency access exists for gate-critical fabric controllers.

MCF-NET-017.objective: Ensure structured cabling and high-density fibre plant are designed to recognised standards for pathways, bend radius, polarity, labelling, density and serviceability so that the physical layer does not become a latent fabric failure source.
MCF-NET-017.requirement: The cabling plant owner shall maintain a cabling design standard for the site covering pathway and containment fill limits, segregation from power, minimum bend radius by cable type, MPO/MTP polarity method, connector cleanliness acceptance, labelling scheme and test acceptance (insertion loss and, where applicable, reflectance), aligned with recognised data-centre cabling standards. The cabling plant owner shall approve deviations, and installers shall be bound to the standard contractually.
MCF-NET-017.unknownEffect: US2: absent standard reduces confidence in physical-layer claims; US3 where NET-018 shows optics failures attributable to cabling.

MCF-NET-018.objective: Ensure transceivers, active and passive cables and NIC/switch firmware are qualified combinations with adequate link budget, so optics do not become a common-mode source of link errors and flaps.
MCF-NET-018.requirement: The network architecture owner shall maintain a qualified-optics matrix listing approved transceiver and cable part numbers, firmware versions, host switch/NIC models and NOS/firmware versions, reach and link-budget class. The fabric operations lead shall reconcile installed optics (from digital diagnostic and CMIS inventory) to the matrix, shall monitor optical diagnostics (Rx/Tx power, temperature, bias, pre-FEC error indicators), and shall quarantine unqualified or degrading optics.
MCF-NET-018.unknownEffect: US3: unqualified optics at scale are a common-mode exposure; escalate to US4 under CG-08 if failure analysis shows lot-level defects.

MCF-NET-019.objective: Ensure physical moves, adds and changes to patching and cross-connects (including in meet-me rooms and carrier demarcations) are authorised, recorded and verified, so that maintenance does not sever redundant paths.
MCF-NET-019.requirement: The network operations manager shall require an approved work order for every physical patch or cross-connect change, specifying both ends, labels, affected path groups and redundancy impact, and shall verify after each change that the link came up on the expected ports and that the cabling records were updated. The network operations manager shall prohibit simultaneous work on members of the same redundant path group unless explicitly approved.
MCF-NET-019.unknownEffect: US3: link events without matching work orders indicate uncontrolled physical change; CG-14 SUPPORTING.

MCF-NET-020.objective: Ensure end-to-end physical and logical path records (port to patch panel to trunk to panel to port, and circuit to route) are complete and accurate enough to support fault isolation, diversity analysis and recovery.
MCF-NET-020.requirement: The network operations manager shall maintain a path-documentation system (DCIM or cable-management database) recording every in-scope link from endpoint port through patch panels, trunks and cross-connects to the far-end port, with labels matching the physical plant and links to circuit IDs for external paths. The network operations manager shall audit a sample of paths physically and electronically at a defined interval and shall correct discrepancies, with an accuracy target set as a capability-profile parameter.
MCF-NET-020.unknownEffect: US3: inaccurate path records undermine diversity (CG-03) and recovery (CG-10) analysis.

MCF-NET-021.objective: Ensure fabric control functions (InfiniBand subnet managers, SDN or EVPN controllers, fabric management platforms, route reflectors) survive single failures and that their loss does not disrupt forwarding beyond tolerance.
MCF-NET-021.requirement: The network architecture owner shall deploy fabric control functions with redundancy (master/standby subnet managers, clustered controllers, redundant route reflectors) placed in separate power and rack fault domains, and shall document the data-plane behaviour when the control function is lost (forwarding continues with stale state, or fails). The fabric operations lead shall test controller and subnet-manager failover at a defined interval and after upgrades and shall confirm forwarding continuity and failover time within tolerance.
MCF-NET-021.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-08 for InfiniBand fabrics where subnet-manager failover is untested.

MCF-NET-022.objective: Ensure network operating system, firmware and configuration across switches, NICs, optics and controllers are held to an approved baseline, changed only through staged and verified rollout, and restorable.
MCF-NET-022.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall maintain a version-controlled source of truth for intended network configuration and an approved baseline of NOS, switch firmware, NIC firmware and driver, optics firmware and controller versions; shall detect configuration and version drift at a defined interval; and shall roll out changes in stages (canary, partial, full) with automated pre- and post-change checks and defined rollback. The network operations manager shall ensure that no single change can be applied simultaneously to both members of a redundant pair or to all planes of a fabric.
MCF-NET-022.unknownEffect: US4: uncontrolled NOS/firmware change on a gate-critical fabric defeats CG-14; CG-08 SUPPORTING.

MCF-NET-023.objective: Ensure network telemetry (counters, streaming telemetry, flow sampling, congestion and buffer metrics) is collected with sufficient coverage, resolution and retention to detect degradation, attribute job slowdowns and support evidence for assurance.
MCF-NET-023.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall collect streaming or polled telemetry from all in-scope switches and NICs covering interface counters, error counters, PFC pause and ECN mark counts, buffer occupancy, and flow sampling, at a resolution sufficient to observe collective-scale events, and shall retain it for the evidence retention period. The fabric operations lead shall monitor telemetry pipeline health and alert on collection gaps.
MCF-NET-023.unknownEffect: US2: gaps reduce confidence of all NET OPERATION claims relying on telemetry.

MCF-NET-024.objective: Ensure time (NTP/PTP), DNS, DHCP, IPAM and network AAA services that fabrics and clusters depend on are redundant, independent of the services they support, and resilient to failure and divergence.
MCF-NET-024.requirement: The network architecture owner shall deploy time sources (with at least two independent references such as GNSS and a holdover oscillator or a remote time service), DNS, DHCP, IPAM and network AAA as redundant services placed in separate fault domains, and shall document every circular dependency between these services and the systems they support. The network operations manager shall monitor time offset, stratum and source agreement, and service availability, and shall test failure of a time source and of a DNS/AAA instance at a defined interval.
MCF-NET-024.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 where a circular dependency could prevent cold start (X19).

MCF-OPS-001.objective: Competent and authorised staff are present or available within response time, every hour of every day, in the numbers and disciplines needed to perform the time-critical tasks of the emergency procedures within the time-to-impact of the failures they address.
MCF-OPS-001.requirement: The operations manager shall define minimum staffing per shift and per discipline (electrical, mechanical/thermal, controls/BMS, NOC/IT infrastructure, security) derived from an emergency task analysis that lists the time-critical manual actions in each EOP (for example manual generator start or transfer, CDU failover, leak isolation, load shedding) and compares their completion time with the time-to-impact from MCF-DEP-003. The operations manager shall roster to that minimum, record every shift that falls below it and the compensating measures, and shall define on-call response times for specialists not on site.
MCF-OPS-001.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-13, CG-10 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-OPS-002.objective: For every Required Function, dependency and operating state, it is clear who operates, who maintains, who monitors, who may approve change, who responds to alarms and who holds emergency decision authority, including across facilities, IT/NOC, tenant and provider teams.
MCF-OPS-002.requirement: The operations manager shall maintain a responsibility and authority matrix for every Required Function and material dependency across NORMAL, MAINTENANCE, EMERGENCY and RECOVERY states, naming the role and current holder (and deputy) for operation, maintenance, monitoring, change approval, alarm response and emergency decisions (for example authority to transfer to generator, shed load, power-cap or drain a cluster, isolate a cooling loop, or invoke an EOP). The matrix shall be consistent with GOV-02 accountability and with provider shared-responsibility records (MCF-DEP-018).
MCF-OPS-002.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-13 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-14 require gate-level evaluation.

MCF-OPS-003.objective: Situational awareness is transferred completely at every shift change: plant and system state, active alarms, open permits and isolations, temporary configurations, deferred maintenance, degraded redundancy, in-progress work and expected events.
MCF-OPS-003.requirement: The shift lead shall conduct and record a structured handover at each shift change using a defined template covering: current operating state per system and redundancy level, active and standing alarms, open permits to work and isolations, temporary configurations and overrides, work in progress and planned work, deferred maintenance with risk, provider or tenant events, and expected events (deliveries, tests, high-load periods). Outgoing and incoming leads shall both sign, and the incoming lead shall verify critical items at the BMS/EPMS/NOC consoles.
MCF-OPS-003.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-04, CG-14 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-OPS-004.objective: Only people assessed as competent, and formally authorised for the task and system, perform hazardous or consequential work, including HV/LV switching, work on battery systems, liquid-cooling and pressurised fluid systems, refrigerants, and control-system changes.
MCF-OPS-004.requirement: The operations manager shall maintain a competence framework defining required knowledge, skills and assessment for each task class, and an authorisation register recording each person's authorisations (for example authorised person and competent person for HV/LV systems, refrigerant handling certification where legally required, liquid-cooling and CDU work, BMS/EPMS engineering), their scope, expiry and assessor. The operations manager shall verify contractor competence and authorisation before work and shall ensure permits (MCF-OPS-007) are issued only to authorised persons.
MCF-OPS-004.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-13 require gate-level evaluation.

MCF-OPS-005.objective: Routine, alarm-response and emergency operations on critical infrastructure are performed from controlled, technically reviewed and current procedures (SOPs, alarm response procedures, EOPs) that match the as-built systems and are available at the point of use.
