MCF-RES-018.requirement: The resilience owner shall plan and execute integrated scenario tests for prioritised scenarios from RES-003 (for example utility loss with generator start and UPS transfer under AI load, cooling string loss at sustained load, fabric plane loss during checkpoint, control-plane loss), measuring capability-level outcomes (job survival, lost work, inference availability, restoration time) as well as system behaviour. The resilience owner shall define test objectives, safety case, abort criteria and success criteria tied to impact tolerances before each test and shall record results and defects.
MCF-RES-018.unknownEffect: US4: CG-10 cannot PASS for an outcome whose prioritised scenarios have never been integrated-tested or analysed from real events.

MCF-RES-019.objective: Ensure decision-makers, operators and providers rehearse response to scenarios that cannot safely be tested live, including cyber-physical, compound and site-loss events.
MCF-RES-019.requirement: The resilience owner shall run tabletop exercises on a defined cycle covering scenarios not testable live, including at least one cyber-physical scenario (for example BMS/EPMS compromise, X05) and one compound event (X20) per cycle, with participation of crisis command, facility, IT, security and key providers. The resilience owner shall record decisions, timings, gaps and actions and shall track actions to closure.
MCF-RES-019.unknownEffect: US2 for confidence; US3 if no cyber-physical scenario was ever exercised.

MCF-RES-020.objective: Ensure that defects and lessons from tests, exercises and real incidents are tracked to closure, reflected in plans and designs, and verified by retest.
MCF-RES-020.requirement: The resilience owner shall maintain a lessons register capturing every defect and lesson from tests, exercises and incidents with owner, due date, and the plan, runbook, design or control affected. The resilience owner shall require retest or equivalent verification before closure of any lesson affecting a gate-critical safeguard and shall report overdue items to governance monthly.
MCF-RES-020.unknownEffect: US3: unclosed gate-critical lessons condition the decision.

MCF-RES-021.objective: Ensure a crisis command structure with defined levels, authority, activation criteria and facilities can take timely decisions during major infrastructure and cyber-physical events.
MCF-RES-021.requirement: The executive sponsor shall establish a crisis command structure with strategic, tactical and operational levels, named primary and alternate role holders, activation criteria, decision authority (including authority to shed load, suspend tenants, invoke alternate capacity and order controlled shutdown), and command facilities and communication channels that remain available when site systems, corporate identity or primary communications fail. The crisis management lead shall demonstrate activation and decision timings in exercises or real events.
MCF-RES-021.unknownEffect: US3; escalates to US4 against CG-13 if no decision authority exists for controlled shutdown.

MCF-RES-022.objective: Ensure timely, accurate communication to customers, tenants, regulators, providers and staff during disruption, consistent with contractual and regulatory notification obligations.
MCF-RES-022.requirement: The crisis management lead shall maintain a communications plan listing stakeholders, notification obligations and deadlines (contractual and regulatory), approved message templates, approval authority and channels that remain available during site and identity failures. The crisis management lead shall record each notification issued during events and exercises with timestamp and approver and shall review timeliness against obligations.
MCF-RES-022.unknownEffect: US2; US3 where regulatory notification timeliness cannot be established.

MCF-RES-023.objective: Ensure changes made under emergency conditions are authorised by defined emergency authority, minimal, recorded, and reconciled back to baseline after the event.
MCF-RES-023.requirement: The change authority shall define an emergency change procedure stating who may authorise emergency changes to infrastructure, OT and control-plane systems, the minimum record to be captured at the time, and the deadline for retrospective review. The recovery manager shall ensure every emergency change is retrospectively reviewed, either reverted or formalised, and that baselines and evidence are updated, and shall report unreconciled emergency changes.

MCF-RES-024.objective: Ensure that after material events the organisation analyses root causes and systemic contributors, adapts design, operations and assurance, and triggers reassessment of affected claims.
MCF-RES-024.requirement: The resilience owner shall require a post-event review within a defined time after every material event, covering timeline, root and contributing causes, safeguard performance against expectation, recovery performance against tolerance, and required adaptations to design, operations, controls and evidence. The resilience owner shall raise reassessment triggers for affected controls and gate results and shall track adaptations to completion.
MCF-RES-024.unknownEffect: US3: unreviewed events may invalidate existing evidence.

MCF-SUP-001.objective: Suppliers of critical equipment and services are shown, before award and at renewal, to have the technical, manufacturing, integration, installation and field-support capability required by the Capability Instance at the site and scale proposed.
MCF-SUP-001.requirement: The procurement lead shall perform and record a capability assessment for each supplier of a critical asset class or service before award and at renewal, covering engineering competence, manufacturing and test capacity (including factory acceptance testing), rack-scale or skid integration capability where applicable, installation and commissioning resources, field-service coverage and response at the site, and references for comparable deployments. A competent engineer shall approve the technical part of the assessment.
MCF-SUP-001.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-002.objective: The financial health, manufacturing footprint, allocation exposure and business-continuity capability of critical suppliers are monitored so that supplier distress or disruption is detected early enough to act.
MCF-SUP-002.requirement: The supplier manager shall monitor each critical supplier at the profile interval for financial distress indicators, manufacturing and logistics concentration (single plant or region), allocation or quota exposure (for example accelerator allocations), sanctions and export-control exposure, and business-continuity arrangements, and shall escalate adverse changes to the capability owner with a proposed treatment.
MCF-SUP-002.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-003.objective: Critical suppliers operate quality management and secure development practices adequate for products that will run, control or protect AI infrastructure, including product security incident response for firmware and control software.
MCF-SUP-003.requirement: The procurement lead shall obtain and evaluate evidence of each critical supplier's quality management system, product security development lifecycle for firmware and control software, product security incident response (PSIRT) and vulnerability disclosure process, and factory test and outgoing quality controls. The procurement lead shall record identified gaps with contract conditions and shall track incoming quality (defects on receipt, early-life failures) for each supplier.
MCF-SUP-003.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-08, CG-15 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-004.objective: Critical sub-tier dependencies behind first-tier suppliers (for example high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging for accelerators, laser and optical components, transformer core steel and bushings, switchgear breaker mechanisms, CDU pumps and heat exchangers, battery cells, controller chipsets, and contract manufacturers) are known well enough to reveal shared sub-tier sources across nominally diverse suppliers.
MCF-SUP-004.requirement: The procurement lead shall obtain, for each critical asset class, disclosure of material sub-tier suppliers and manufacturing locations from first-tier suppliers, record them in the dependency graph, and identify sub-tier sources shared across nominally diverse first-tier suppliers. Where a supplier declines disclosure, the procurement lead shall record an UNKNOWN Record and the capability owner shall decide on treatment.
MCF-SUP-004.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned.

MCF-SUP-005.objective: Contracts for maintenance, support and supply of critical systems contain measurable service levels (response, on-site attendance, restore, parts availability, RMA turnaround) that are consistent with the Service Outcome and recovery tolerances.
MCF-SUP-005.requirement: The supplier manager shall ensure each critical support or maintenance contract states measurable service levels with units, measurement points, exclusions and escalation, and shall document that each service level is consistent with the time-to-impact and recovery tolerances in DEP-003 and CAP-02. Where contracted levels are inconsistent, the capability owner shall record the gap and its treatment (on-site spares, resident engineers, alternative supplier).
MCF-SUP-005.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10, CG-13 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-006.objective: The owner has contractual rights to obtain the evidence needed to assess supplier-provided and provider-operated functions: test and commissioning records, maintenance records, firmware SBOMs and release notes, telemetry access, incident RCAs, audit reports and access for witness testing and audit.
MCF-SUP-006.requirement: The supplier manager shall ensure that each critical supplier and provider contract grants rights to the evidence listed in the AIDCF-008 control evidence profiles relevant to the supplied function, within stated timescales and formats, including rights to witness tests and to audit or receive independent assurance reports, and shall record any evidence the supplier will not provide as an UNKNOWN Record against the affected controls.
MCF-SUP-006.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-007.objective: Suppliers and providers notify the owner promptly of incidents, vulnerabilities, field notices, recalls, allocation changes and planned changes that could affect supplied functions, and the notifications reach the people who must act.
MCF-SUP-007.requirement: The supplier manager shall ensure critical supplier and provider contracts define notification obligations and timescales for incidents, security vulnerabilities, field notices and recalls, planned maintenance and changes, and allocation or end-of-life changes, and shall operate a monitored intake (shared mailbox, portal subscription, ticket integration) that routes notifications to the responsible owner. The supplier manager shall test the intake path at the profile interval.
MCF-SUP-007.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03, CG-15 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-008.objective: The owner can exit or replace a critical supplier or provider without losing the ability to operate, maintain or recover critical systems, including access to configuration, control logic, data, documentation, licences, spares and transition assistance.
MCF-SUP-008.requirement: The supplier manager shall ensure each critical contract provides exit and transition rights proportionate to the dependency, including export of configuration and operational data in usable formats, ownership or escrow of control logic and configuration for programmable controllers, perpetual or transition licences for software required to operate installed equipment, option to purchase spares and tools, documentation hand-over, and transition assistance for a stated period. The capability owner shall maintain an exit plan for each sole-source or high-concentration supplier.
MCF-SUP-008.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-009.objective: Critical components (protection devices, circuit breakers and trip units, relays, UPS modules and batteries, accelerators and boards, memory, optics, NICs/DPUs, storage media, controllers and sensors) are purchased only from the OEM or OEM-authorised channels, so that counterfeit, grey-market, refurbished-as-new and tampered parts are excluded at source.
MCF-SUP-009.requirement: The procurement lead shall maintain an approved source list for each critical component class naming the OEM and authorised distributors, shall configure purchasing controls so that orders for critical classes can be placed only with approved sources, and shall require documented engineering approval and enhanced inspection (MCF-SUP-010) for any exception, such as broker purchase of obsolete parts.
MCF-SUP-009.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-08, CG-04 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-010.objective: Counterfeit, cloned, remarked or tampered components are detected at receipt, before installation, by inspection and test proportionate to risk, and suspect parts are quarantined and reported.
MCF-SUP-010.requirement: The receiving and engineering leads shall operate a risk-based incoming inspection for critical component classes, including label, serial and packaging verification against OEM records, physical inspection, and where risk warrants electrical or functional testing (for example protection device trip testing, optics DOM/EEPROM checks, firmware identity checks on boards). Suspect items shall be quarantined, reported to the OEM and, where required, to the relevant authority, and shall not be installed until cleared.
MCF-SUP-010.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-04, CG-08 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-011.objective: High-value and integrity-sensitive equipment (accelerator systems, storage media, network gear, controllers, spare boards) is under recorded custody from the factory or integrator to installation, so that theft, substitution and tampering in transit or staging are prevented or detected.
MCF-SUP-011.requirement: The logistics lead shall require tamper-evident packaging and seals for critical shipments, recorded hand-offs between factory, freight forwarder, carrier and site, secure staging areas with access control, and receipt verification of seals and serials against the advance shipping notice. Breaks in custody or seal anomalies shall be recorded as security events and the affected items quarantined pending inspection.
MCF-SUP-011.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-08 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-012.objective: Critical installed components can be traced by serial number, part number, revision and firmware to their location and the functions they support, quickly enough to act on a field notice, recall or vulnerability before it causes harm.
MCF-SUP-012.requirement: The asset manager shall record serial, part number, hardware revision and firmware version for critical components (accelerators and boards, NICs/DPUs, optics, switch line cards, storage media, breaker trip units, relays, UPS modules, batteries, CDU pumps and controllers) in the asset register linked to location and Required Function, and shall demonstrate at the profile interval, by exercise, that all units affected by a given notice can be identified within the target time.
MCF-SUP-012.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-08, CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-013.objective: Every firmware, software and configuration package deployed to AI and facility infrastructure (accelerator and board firmware, BMC/BIOS, NIC/DPU firmware, switch OS, storage controller software, drivers and runtime stacks, UPS/PDU/ATS firmware, BMS/EPMS software, CDU and PLC logic) comes from an authenticated source with release notes and component inventory, and is held in a controlled internal repository before deployment.
MCF-SUP-013.requirement: The platform and control-system owners shall obtain releases only from authenticated OEM channels, record for each release its origin, version, hash, release notes and software bill of materials where available, store it in a controlled repository with access control and integrity protection, and deploy only from that repository. Releases for programmable facility controllers shall be held with the same controls as IT firmware.
MCF-SUP-013.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-15, CG-14 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-014.objective: Firmware and software are cryptographically verified before installation and, where the platform supports it, at boot, so that modified or malicious images are rejected.
MCF-SUP-014.requirement: The platform and control-system owners shall verify OEM signatures (or, where signing is unavailable, OEM-published hashes obtained over an authenticated channel) before staging any release to the repository and before deployment, shall enable platform secure-boot and firmware-signature enforcement where supported (for example on BMCs, accelerators, NICs/DPUs, switches), and shall record device classes that cannot enforce signatures with compensating controls. The owners shall demonstrate rejection of an unsigned or altered image on a non-production device for each enforcing device class.
MCF-SUP-014.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-15, CG-08 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-015.objective: Firmware, driver and software updates are deployed only in combinations that are validated as compatible, and are rolled out in stages aligned to fault domains so that a defective release cannot defeat redundant capacity at once.
MCF-SUP-015.requirement: The platform owner shall maintain a compatibility matrix for interdependent components (for example accelerator firmware, driver and runtime libraries, NIC/DPU firmware, switch OS, BMC/BIOS, storage client; and for facility systems UPS firmware and EPMS, CDU controller and BMS integration), shall test each new combination on a representative non-production environment, and shall deploy through staged waves where each wave is confined to one fault domain and passes defined health criteria before the next begins. Redundant members of a group shall not be updated in the same wave.
MCF-SUP-015.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-14, CG-08, CG-09 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-016.objective: Vulnerabilities disclosed by suppliers for firmware, OT controllers and AI infrastructure components are triaged, and fixes or compensating controls are applied within timescales proportionate to exposure and consequence.
MCF-SUP-016.requirement: The security owner shall track supplier advisories for in-scope products, triage each against the asset register and exposure (network reachability, privilege required), assign a remediation target based on severity and consequence, and record either patch deployment through change control or a compensating control with approved exception. The security owner shall report remediation performance to the accountable owner.
MCF-SUP-016.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-15 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-017.objective: Spares for critical assets are held in the quantity, location and condition needed to restore Required Functions within tolerance, based on failure behaviour, installed population, repair time and resupply lead time, rather than on habit or warranty terms.
MCF-SUP-017.requirement: The maintenance manager shall define a spares strategy for each critical asset class (for example UPS modules and capacitors, battery strings, breakers and trip units, protection relays, generator starter motors and controllers, CDU pumps and controllers, chiller compressors and VFDs, transformer bushings or, where justified, a strategic spare transformer, accelerator trays or boards, NICs, optics, switch line cards, storage drives), stating stock level, location (on site, regional, OEM-held), basis (population, failure rate, MTTR target, lead time) and condition-maintenance requirements for stored spares. The maintenance manager shall reconcile stock to records at the profile interval and replenish below-minimum stock as a tracked action.
MCF-SUP-017.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10, CG-05, CG-06 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-018.objective: Lead times for long-lead equipment (power transformers, MV switchgear, generators, UPS systems, chillers and dry coolers, CDUs, accelerator systems, high-speed optics, switch hardware) are known, tracked and compared with recovery and growth needs, so that both failure replacement and planned expansion are realistic.
MCF-SUP-018.requirement: The procurement lead shall maintain current quoted and observed lead times for each long-lead equipment class, including manufacturing slot reservations and logistics time, and the capability owner shall compare each with (a) the recovery tolerance for loss of an installed unit and (b) the capacity growth schedule, recording each case where lead time exceeds tolerance or schedule with a treatment (strategic spare, slot reservation, framework order, design change) or acceptance.
MCF-SUP-018.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10, CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-019.objective: The logistics and labour needed for recovery and urgent replacement (heavy-haul transport and route permits for transformers and generators, port and customs clearance, cross-border movement under export controls, emergency fuel delivery, and mobilisation of specialist labour such as HV jointers, commissioning engineers, OEM field engineers and liquid-cooling technicians) can be delivered within recovery tolerance under declared regional disruption.
MCF-SUP-019.requirement: The recovery owner shall identify the logistics and specialist-labour prerequisites for each recovery scenario involving replacement of long-lead equipment or emergency resupply, shall secure them through contracts or pre-arrangements (heavy-haul contractors, route surveys, customs brokers, export licences, fuel priority, labour call-off agreements), and shall validate them by exercise or documented precedent at the profile interval, including under at least one regional-disruption assumption.
MCF-SUP-019.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10, CG-05 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-020.objective: End-of-sale, end-of-support and obsolescence of critical hardware, firmware and control platforms (PLCs, BMS/EPMS controllers and servers, UPS models, protection relays, accelerator generations, switch OS, storage platforms) are anticipated and managed before support or parts cease.
MCF-SUP-020.requirement: The asset manager shall maintain a lifecycle register recording vendor end-of-sale and end-of-support dates for critical assets, shall review it at the profile interval, and shall ensure each asset reaching end-of-support within the planning horizon has an approved treatment (refresh, last-time buy, extended support, third-party support with compensating controls) recorded before the date.
MCF-SUP-020.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-021.objective: Every person from an OEM, integrator, maintenance contractor or managed-service provider who can access facility or AI infrastructure, remotely or on site, is individually identified and authenticated; shared vendor accounts and default credentials do not exist.
MCF-SUP-021.requirement: The security owner shall require that all third-party support access to BMS/EPMS, CDU and PLC systems, UPS and switchgear management interfaces, BMCs, cluster managers, fabric and storage controllers uses named individual identities, verified by the supplier and registered by the owner, with multi-factor authentication for remote access. Shared, generic and default vendor accounts shall be disabled or, where technically unavoidable, vaulted with per-use checkout bound to a named person and recorded as an exception.
MCF-SUP-021.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-15 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-13 require gate-level evaluation.

MCF-SUP-022.objective: Third-party remote access to facility and AI infrastructure is off by default and is enabled only for an approved, time-limited, asset-scoped session linked to a work order or change.
MCF-SUP-022.requirement: The facility operator shall ensure that third-party remote access paths are disabled by default and are activated only on approval by an authorised owner representative, for a stated duration and set of target assets, referencing an approved ticket or change, through a brokered access gateway. Access shall be deactivated automatically at expiry. Emergency activation shall follow a defined path with retrospective review within the profile time.
MCF-SUP-022.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-15 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-14 require gate-level evaluation.

MCF-SUP-023.objective: Third-party sessions on control-plane and OT systems are recorded and, for high-consequence systems, monitored in real time by a competent owner representative able to terminate the session.
MCF-SUP-023.requirement: The security owner shall record all third-party sessions to in-scope control-plane and OT systems (keystroke or screen recording through the access broker where feasible), shall require live monitoring by a competent owner representative for sessions to systems designated high-consequence (for example EPMS switching, BMS/CDU control, protection relay configuration), and shall retain recordings for the profile period. The owner representative shall have and use the means to terminate a session.
MCF-SUP-023.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-15 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SUP-024.objective: Third-party logical and physical access is revoked promptly when no longer needed and is periodically recertified, so that access does not outlive the person, contract or task.
MCF-SUP-024.requirement: The security owner shall revoke third-party logical access, credentials, tokens and physical badges within the profile time of contract end, personnel departure notified by the supplier, or task completion, and shall recertify all third-party access with the owning system owner at the profile interval, removing any access not positively confirmed.
MCF-SUP-024.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-15, CG-13 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

MCF-SEC-001.objective: Ensure every person who can observe, configure or command facility OT, infrastructure management planes or AI control planes is uniquely identified, strongly authenticated and lifecycle-managed, with no shared or orphaned accounts.
MCF-SEC-001.requirement: The identity and access manager shall ensure that every human identity with access to BMS, EPMS, CDU and PLC engineering workstations and HMIs, BMC/Redfish interfaces, network devices, hypervisor and Kubernetes control planes, cluster managers and storage controllers is individually attributable, uses phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication where the system supports it (with compensating controls recorded where it does not, for example legacy HMIs), and is joined, moved and removed through an authoritative identity source within defined deadlines. The OT security owner shall maintain an inventory of OT systems that cannot integrate with central identity and the compensating controls applied.
MCF-SEC-001.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-15 where accounts on BMS/EPMS or BMC planes cannot be enumerated.

MCF-SEC-002.objective: Ensure machine identities (service accounts, API tokens, certificates, workload identities, node and device identities) used by automation, controllers and agents are inventoried, scoped, rotated and, for hardware, anchored in a root of trust with attestation.
MCF-SEC-002.requirement: The platform security lead shall maintain an inventory of machine identities with access to in-scope infrastructure, including owner, purpose, scope, credential type, rotation interval and expiry, and shall prohibit long-lived static credentials for consequential authority where short-lived or certificate-based credentials are supported. The platform security lead shall require hardware-rooted identity (for example TPM or device identity certificates) and boot or firmware attestation (for example via SPDM or TPM quotes) for accelerator nodes, BMCs and fabric devices that support it, and shall gate cluster admission on successful attestation.
MCF-SEC-002.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-15 where unscoped machine credentials with OT or control-plane write authority exist.

MCF-SEC-003.objective: Ensure privileged and consequential authority over facility OT, BMC/Redfish, network, hypervisor/Kubernetes, cluster manager and storage control planes is least-privilege, brokered, time-bound and monitored, so no single compromised identity can command cross-domain infrastructure.
MCF-SEC-003.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall define privileged roles by authority action (observe, configure, command, bypass, update, revoke, recover, per AIDCF-005) and by domain, shall prohibit standing cross-domain privileged roles (for example a single role with write access to both BMS/EPMS and cluster control planes) except as approved break-glass, and shall broker privileged sessions through a privileged access management (PAM) system or jump hosts providing just-in-time elevation, session recording and approval for command and bypass actions. The infrastructure security owner shall test at a defined interval that privilege boundaries hold, including that elevation requires approval and that sessions are recorded.
MCF-SEC-003.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while consequential cross-domain authority is unanalysed or untested.

MCF-SEC-004.objective: Ensure emergency accounts and procedures across OT, infrastructure and control planes work when central identity fails, are protected against misuse, and every use is reviewed.
MCF-SEC-004.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall govern break-glass arrangements for all in-scope domains: inventory of emergency accounts, storage under dual control with an offline copy outside the failure domains they recover, use triggers, notification on use, maximum duration, mandatory post-use review and credential rotation. The infrastructure security owner shall verify at a defined interval that break-glass retrieval and login work with the primary identity provider and vault unavailable, and shall review all uses.
MCF-SEC-004.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 if no tested emergency access exists for recovery-critical control planes.

MCF-SEC-005.objective: Ensure building management, electrical power monitoring, CDU and PLC/SCADA systems that monitor and command power and cooling are secured to a target security level appropriate to their consequence, so compromise or misuse cannot defeat electrical or thermal continuity.
MCF-SEC-005.requirement: The OT security owner shall perform a security risk assessment for BMS, EPMS, CDU controllers, PLCs, SCADA servers, historians and engineering workstations using a zone-and-conduit approach consistent with ISA/IEC 62443, assign a target security level (SL-T) to each zone, and implement countermeasures across the foundational requirement areas (identification and authentication, use control, system integrity, data confidentiality, restricted data flow, timely response to events, resource availability). The facility owner shall ensure that safety-instrumented and protection functions (electrical protection relays, emergency shutdown, hardwired interlocks) are independent of BMS/EPMS networks, and the OT security owner shall verify by test that unauthorised write or command attempts against controllers are blocked or detected and that controllers fail to a defined safe state on loss of supervisory communication.
MCF-SEC-005.unknownEffect: US4: CG-07 cannot PASS while BMS/EPMS write/command exposure or fail-safe behaviour is unverified (scenario X05).

MCF-SEC-006.objective: Ensure the AI control plane (Kubernetes or HPC scheduler, cluster manager, provisioning and image services, hypervisor managers) cannot be used to gain unbounded authority over compute, data and connected infrastructure.
MCF-SEC-006.requirement: The platform security lead shall harden each cluster manager and control plane to a documented benchmark (for example CIS Kubernetes Benchmark where applicable), restrict API server and scheduler administrative access to brokered privileged paths, enforce admission control that blocks privileged containers, host-namespace access and unapproved images on accelerator nodes, protect control-plane state stores (for example etcd) with encryption and access restriction, and separate tenant-facing from infrastructure-administrative interfaces. The platform security lead shall test at a defined interval that a tenant or workload identity cannot escalate to node, cluster-admin or BMC authority.
MCF-SEC-006.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while tenant-to-infrastructure escalation paths are untested.

MCF-SEC-007.objective: Ensure fabric controllers, subnet managers, SDN controllers and network automation platforms are protected so that their compromise cannot reconfigure, partition or blackhole fabrics.
MCF-SEC-007.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall ensure fabric controllers, subnet managers and network automation platforms are reachable only from the management zone, use individually attributable and brokered administrative access, authenticate southbound connections to devices (for example certificate-based gNMI/NETCONF), protect fabric security keys (for example InfiniBand management and partition keys), and log all configuration actions to the security telemetry platform. The fabric operations lead shall reconcile controller access configuration to this requirement at a defined interval.
MCF-SEC-007.unknownEffect: US3: unknown controller exposure conditions CG-15 and CG-08 claims.

MCF-SEC-008.objective: Ensure storage management planes cannot be used to destroy, encrypt or exfiltrate training data, checkpoints and model artefacts, and that destructive operations require additional protection.
MCF-SEC-008.requirement: The storage platform owner shall restrict storage controller and management interfaces to the management zone with brokered privileged access, shall require multi-person approval or delayed execution for destructive operations (volume or bucket deletion, snapshot or retention policy reduction, replication break), shall protect immutable recovery copies with retention locks that administrators cannot shorten, and shall log management actions to security telemetry.
MCF-SEC-008.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 where checkpoint recovery copies lack immutability.

MCF-SEC-009.objective: Ensure the facility OT, infrastructure management, AI control-plane, tenant and corporate environments are partitioned into security zones with defined conduits, so that compromise in one zone cannot reach consequential authority in another.
MCF-SEC-009.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall maintain a zone-and-conduit model covering facility OT (BMS, EPMS, CDU, PLC, fire and physical security integrations), infrastructure management (BMC, PDU, switch management, OOB), AI control planes, storage management, tenant and corporate networks and external connections, with each conduit's permitted flows, protocols and direction, and the security level target per zone. The OT security owner shall reconcile the as-built network (firewall rules, VLAN/VRF configuration, physical links, wireless and cellular devices) to the model at a defined interval and after change, and shall record every undocumented path (including dual-homed hosts and vendor-installed modems) as a Finding.
MCF-SEC-009.unknownEffect: US4: CG-07 cannot PASS while an undocumented path into a power or cooling control zone cannot be ruled out.

MCF-SEC-010.objective: Ensure management planes (BMC/IPMI/Redfish, switch management, PDU, hypervisor and Kubernetes administrative APIs, storage management) are segmented so that tenant, workload and corporate networks cannot reach them, and so that one management plane cannot be used to pivot to another.
MCF-SEC-010.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall segment each management plane into its own zone, shall disable insecure management protocols (for example IPMI over LAN where Redfish is available, unauthenticated SNMP versions, Telnet), shall restrict BMC access to brokered administrative paths, and shall prevent host operating systems from reaching their own or other BMCs over the network except where required and approved. The infrastructure security owner shall test at a defined interval from representative tenant, workload and corporate vantage points that management interfaces are unreachable and that pivoting between management planes is blocked.
MCF-SEC-010.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while BMC or control-plane reachability from tenant workloads is untested.

MCF-SEC-011.objective: Ensure conduits between zones are enforced by managed boundary devices whose rule sets are minimal, reviewed and monitored, including industrial DMZs, unidirectional gateways and API gateways for automation.
MCF-SEC-011.requirement: The security operations manager shall operate boundary devices on every conduit in the zone model with deny-by-default rule sets, documented business justification and owner for each rule, review of rules at a defined interval, removal of unused rules, and logging of denied and permitted consequential flows to security telemetry. The OT security owner shall use unidirectional or protocol-break gateways where the zone model requires one-way data export from power and cooling control zones.
MCF-SEC-011.unknownEffect: US3: unreviewed rules condition CG-07/CG-15 evaluation.

MCF-SEC-012.objective: Ensure all remote access to OT, infrastructure management and AI control planes, especially by vendors and OEMs, is brokered, approved per session, time-bound, monitored and revocable.
MCF-SEC-012.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall permit remote access to in-scope systems only through a managed remote-access gateway that enforces individual identity, MFA, per-session approval by the system owner for vendor and OEM access, time limits, session recording and the ability to terminate sessions in real time, and shall prohibit persistent vendor connections, vendor-installed remote-access tools and modems. The OT security owner shall require that remote sessions to power and cooling control systems with write or command capability are supervised by an on-site or on-shift authorised operator.
MCF-SEC-012.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while an unmanaged remote path into OT or control planes cannot be ruled out.

MCF-SEC-013.objective: Ensure OT controllers, BMCs, accelerator nodes, NICs, switches and control-plane hosts run hardened configurations and integrity-verified firmware with secure boot, so that tampered or insecure states are prevented or detected.
MCF-SEC-013.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall define secure configuration baselines for each in-scope device class, including disabled unused services, credential policy, logging, and for firmware-bearing devices the approved signed firmware versions, secure boot enablement, firmware rollback protection and measured boot where supported. The platform security lead shall verify compliance with the baseline at a defined interval using automated assessment or attestation and shall record non-compliant devices as Findings.
MCF-SEC-013.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-07 where OT controller firmware integrity is unknown.

MCF-SEC-014.objective: Ensure vulnerabilities in OT, infrastructure management, firmware and AI control-plane components are identified, prioritised by exploitability and infrastructure consequence, and remediated or mitigated within defined times.
MCF-SEC-014.requirement: The security operations manager shall maintain vulnerability visibility for all in-scope asset classes (including passive or vendor-advisory-based identification for OT assets that cannot be actively scanned), shall prioritise using exploitation evidence (for example known-exploited catalogues) and infrastructure consequence (reachability to CG-05/CG-06/CG-07/CG-15 authority), and shall meet remediation or mitigation times defined per priority. The security operations manager shall report overdue items to governance.
MCF-SEC-014.unknownEffect: US3: unknown vulnerability state conditions CG-07/CG-15 evaluation.

MCF-SEC-015.objective: Ensure security patches and firmware updates to OT and infrastructure are tested for compatibility and operational impact, staged to avoid common-mode failure, and applied within defined times.
MCF-SEC-015.requirement: The change authority shall require that patches and firmware updates to OT controllers, BMCs, NICs, switches, accelerator nodes and control planes are tested on representative test systems, approved by the system owner and, for OT, the vendor where required, applied in stages that never update all redundant members or all fault domains simultaneously, and verified after application with rollback available. The security operations manager shall measure patch latency against defined targets.

MCF-SEC-016.objective: Ensure security exceptions (unpatchable OT, legacy protocols, missing MFA) are approved by appropriate authority, time-bound and backed by verified compensating controls.
MCF-SEC-016.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall maintain a security exception register for in-scope systems recording the deviation, risk assessment including infrastructure consequence, compensating controls, approver at the authority level required by consequence, and expiry. The infrastructure security owner shall verify compensating controls are in place before approval and at renewal.
MCF-SEC-016.unknownEffect: US3: unapproved deviations condition the decision.

MCF-SEC-017.objective: Ensure security-relevant logs and events from OT, management planes, control planes, remote access and identity systems are collected centrally with integrity, time synchronisation and retention sufficient for detection and investigation.
MCF-SEC-017.requirement: The security operations manager shall collect security telemetry from identity providers, PAM, remote-access gateways, boundary devices, BMCs, network devices, fabric controllers, cluster managers, storage controllers and OT passive monitoring (including controller write and program-change events), with time synchronised to NET-024 sources, integrity protection, and retention per the evidence retention class, and shall monitor source health and alert on silent sources.
MCF-SEC-017.unknownEffect: US2 for confidence; US3 where OT write events are not visible.

MCF-SEC-018.objective: Ensure detection of anomalous or malicious behaviour against infrastructure authority, including unexpected OT writes, BMC firmware operations, mass configuration changes, privilege escalation and anomalous automation actions.
MCF-SEC-018.requirement: The security operations manager shall maintain detection use cases mapped to infrastructure threat scenarios (for example ATT&CK for ICS techniques and AIDCF-004 scenarios X05, X08, X15), covering unexpected controller writes or program changes, BMC firmware update or power commands outside change windows, mass configuration pushes, privilege escalation, anomalous remote sessions and automation acting outside its scope, and shall validate detection effectiveness by safe simulation at a defined interval.
MCF-SEC-018.unknownEffect: US3: untested detection reduces CG-15 confidence.

MCF-SEC-019.objective: Ensure cyber and cyber-physical incidents affecting infrastructure can be contained without causing unsafe states or unnecessary loss of AI service, with pre-approved containment actions and safety-coordinated decision-making.
MCF-SEC-019.requirement: The security operations manager shall maintain incident playbooks for infrastructure scenarios (BMS/EPMS compromise, BMC compromise, control-plane compromise, malicious automation, vendor account compromise) that define pre-approved containment actions (credential revocation, conduit closure, session termination, controller isolation to local or manual control), the safety checks required before each action, and the decision authority. The facility owner shall ensure that OT containment actions are coordinated with facility operations so that isolating supervisory control does not remove cooling or power continuity, and the security operations manager shall exercise the playbooks at a defined interval.
MCF-SEC-019.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-09 for cyber-physical scenarios with no exercised containment.

MCF-SEC-020.objective: Ensure that evidence needed to investigate infrastructure incidents (logs, controller programs, firmware images, session recordings) is preserved with chain of custody and that collection does not endanger operations.
MCF-SEC-020.requirement: The security operations manager shall define forensic collection procedures for each in-scope system class, including OT controllers and BMCs, specifying what to collect, how to collect safely, and chain-of-custody requirements, and shall ensure retention and legal hold capability for telemetry and session recordings. The OT security owner shall ensure baseline copies of controller programs and firmware hashes are available for comparison.
MCF-SEC-020.unknownEffect: US2: affects investigation confidence; US3 if baseline programs are absent.

MCF-SEC-021.objective: Ensure every AI agent, automation pipeline and closed-loop controller that can act on infrastructure has an explicit, bounded and inventoried authority scope, so that tool-mediated actions cannot exceed what the owner approved.
MCF-SEC-021.requirement: The automation owner shall register every agent, automation and closed-loop control that can observe, configure, command, bypass, update or recover infrastructure (including AIOps remediation, cooling optimisation loops, power capping, network automation and AI agents with tool access), stating its effective identity, tools and APIs, target systems, permitted actions, rate and magnitude limits, operating states in which it may act, and its human owner. The infrastructure security owner shall reconcile registered scope with effective permissions at a defined interval and shall prohibit any automation from holding cross-domain command or bypass authority without approval under SEC-003.
MCF-SEC-021.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while any automation or agent with consequential infrastructure authority is unregistered or unreconciled.

MCF-SEC-022.objective: Ensure consequential automated or agent-initiated infrastructure actions require human approval proportionate to consequence, and that approvals cannot be bypassed.
MCF-SEC-022.requirement: The automation owner shall classify each automated action by consequence and reversibility and shall require human approval (single or dual) for actions above the defined threshold, such as OT setpoint or mode changes beyond limits, power-cycling beyond one fault domain, firmware updates, fabric-wide configuration pushes and destructive storage operations. The infrastructure security owner shall verify by test that approval cannot be bypassed by the automation's own identity.
MCF-SEC-022.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-15 where OT command approvals are self-enforced by the agent.

MCF-SEC-023.objective: Ensure that only explicitly allowlisted commands, write operations and parameter ranges can be issued to power, cooling and critical infrastructure controllers by any automated or remote actor, enforced at a point the actor cannot modify.
MCF-SEC-023.requirement: The OT security owner shall enforce, at a boundary or broker the actor cannot modify (for example an OT protocol-aware gateway, a command broker or controller-level write protection), an allowlist of permitted commands, registers or objects, and parameter ranges for writes to BMS, EPMS, CDU and PLC systems from automation, agents and remote sessions, and shall block or require approval for anything outside the list. The OT security owner shall test at a defined interval that out-of-list writes and out-of-range values are blocked and alarmed.
MCF-SEC-023.unknownEffect: US4: CG-07 cannot PASS while automated or remote writes to power/cooling controllers are unrestricted or untested.

MCF-SEC-024.objective: Ensure automated or agent-initiated infrastructure changes can be detected, halted and reversed to a known-safe state quickly, including when the automation itself has failed or been compromised.
MCF-SEC-024.requirement: The automation owner shall provide, for every registered automation and agent, a kill switch that halts its actions without depending on the automation itself, a record of actions taken sufficient to reverse them, and a defined safe state (for example last approved setpoints, previous configuration) for each target. The automation owner shall test at a defined interval that the kill switch halts actions within target time and that rollback restores the safe state, coordinating OT rollback with facility operations.
MCF-SEC-024.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-15 for automations with OT command authority lacking tested halt.

MCF-EVA-001.objective: Ensure that every in-scope control has an Evidence Requirement profile expressed in the AIDCF-008 vocabulary (classes E1-E7, quality floor, sufficiency floor, state and period coverage, independence), and that any local evidence subtypes map unambiguously to those classes.
MCF-EVA-001.requirement: The evidence lead shall maintain, for every in-scope control, an Evidence Requirement profile using the AIDCF-008 classes, quality dimensions (P, F, C, R, T, I), sufficiency levels and control profile tiers, strengthened where the capability profile or criticality requires and never weakened below the registry profile. The evidence lead shall maintain a mapping of every local evidence subtype (for example 'EPMS waveform capture', 'CDU trend export', 'fabric link error report') to exactly one AIDCF-008 class.
MCF-EVA-001.unknownEffect: US3 Material: evidence sufficiency judgements for affected controls lack a stated basis; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

MCF-EVA-002.objective: Ensure that for every Evidence Requirement there is a named source owner responsible for producing the evidence, so that requests reach someone with access and authority, and missing evidence is attributable.
MCF-EVA-002.requirement: The evidence lead shall assign, for each Evidence Requirement in an assessment, a source owner (person or role in the owner, operator or provider organisation) responsible for producing the evidence by the requested date, and shall record each request, response, delay and refusal in the evidence request record. Unfulfilled requests at the response deadline shall be escalated to the capability owner and recorded as UNKNOWN where unresolved.
MCF-EVA-002.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: attribution of missing evidence uncertain; confidence ceiling CONF-2 for affected controls

MCF-EVA-003.objective: Ensure that accepted evidence is held in a repository that assigns immutable identifiers, records the mandatory AIDCF-008 metadata, produces an EvidenceManifest with hashes for each Evidence Package, and supports retrieval of exactly the evidence a decision relied on.
MCF-EVA-003.requirement: The evidence lead shall operate an evidence repository in which every Evidence Object has an immutable identifier, the mandatory metadata defined in AIDCF-008 (including source, collector, custodian, observation time, collection time, scope, state, classification, integrity value and lifecycle state), and conditional metadata for test, telemetry, configuration, human, external and derived evidence. The tool owner shall configure the repository to generate an EvidenceManifest with content hashes for each Evidence Package and to freeze the manifest referenced by each Assurance Decision.
MCF-EVA-003.unknownEffect: US3 Material: reproducibility of decisions uncertain; affected decisions treated as integrity-uncertain for CG-11

MCF-EVA-004.objective: Ensure that assurance evidence is retained according to its retention class, protected according to its classification, preserved under legal hold, and recoverable after loss of the repository, so that decisions remain reviewable and challengeable throughout their validity.
MCF-EVA-004.requirement: The evidence lead shall assign each Evidence Object a retention class (R0-R5) and a classification level, define retention periods by legal, contractual and decision-validity requirements, apply legal holds when instructed, and record authorised destruction. The tool owner shall back up the repository, including manifests and custody logs, to a separate fault domain and shall test restoration at the restoration test interval, verifying hashes and custody logs after restore.
MCF-EVA-004.unknownEffect: US3 Material: future challenge and reassessment of decisions may be impossible; decision condition recorded

MCF-EVA-005.objective: Ensure that every accepted Evidence Object has an established origin, authority and collection lineage, including derived and AI-assisted evidence whose sources, transformation and human review are recorded, so that no conclusion rests on evidence of unknown origin.
MCF-EVA-005.requirement: The lead assessor shall ensure that, before an Evidence Object is accepted, its source, collector, collection activity and authority are recorded and verified; that derived evidence records source Evidence IDs, query or script and version, assumptions and reviewer; and that AI-assisted extraction, summarisation or classification is recorded with model and version, process record and the accountable human review, and is treated as candidate evidence that does not corroborate its own sources.
MCF-EVA-005.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected results may become UNKNOWN (U6); CG-11 evaluation records the gap

MCF-EVA-006.objective: Ensure that alteration of evidence or loss of custody is detected, so that evidence supporting gates and decisions can be shown to be the evidence originally collected.
MCF-EVA-006.requirement: The evidence lead shall ensure that every Evidence Object supporting a gate result or Assurance Decision has an integrity value computed at collection, an integrity level (I0-I5) assigned, and a custody log; that integrity values are re-verified before decision issue and on retrieval for challenge or reassessment; and that integrity failures are recorded, investigated and the affected evidence withdrawn from support. The evidence lead shall test detection at least once per integrity test interval by a controlled tamper exercise on test objects.
MCF-EVA-006.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected evidence treated as U7; dependent gate results may become UNKNOWN under CG-11

MCF-EVA-007.objective: Ensure that each Evidence Object is rated for fitness to the precise assertion and for reliability of its method and source, with rationale, so that reliable but irrelevant evidence (for example a design document cited for an operation claim) does not support a result.
MCF-EVA-007.requirement: The lead assessor shall ensure that every Evidence Object used to support a Control Assessment is rated on all six AIDCF-008 quality dimensions with rationale, that the fitness (F) rating considers subject, criterion, claim type, configuration and operating state, that the reliability (R) rating considers method repeatability and corroboration, and that a second assessor independently re-rates a sample with differences resolved and recorded.
MCF-EVA-007.unknownEffect: US3 Material: result support uncertain; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

MCF-EVA-008.objective: Ensure that evidence is current for the state asserted and covers the required population, locations, period, operating states and scenarios, so that a result is not extrapolated beyond what the evidence represents.
MCF-EVA-008.requirement: The lead assessor shall ensure that each Evidence Object used to support a result is checked against the AIDCF-008 freshness basis for its category and against any material change since collection, and that each Control Assessment records coverage across entity, population, location, time, operating state, scenario, tenant or workload, and dependency dimensions, with gaps recorded as U3 or U5 UNKNOWN Records.
MCF-EVA-008.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected results may be STALE; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

MCF-EVA-009.objective: Ensure that each assessment answers a precisely stated decision question (for example 'Can Capability Instance X sustain training goodput within tolerance through loss of one CDU per pod, as of date D?') that names the Capability Instance, Service Outcomes, tolerances, operating states, intended users and prohibited interpretations.
MCF-EVA-009.requirement: The decision authority shall approve, before fieldwork begins, a decision question for each assessment that states the Capability Instance, the Service Outcomes and tolerances in question, the operating states, the as-of date or period, the intended users and use, and the interpretations the conclusion shall not support. The lead assessor shall frame the assurance case top claim from the approved decision question and shall obtain re-approval if the question changes during the assessment.
MCF-EVA-009.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: decision question undefined; CG-01 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE

MCF-EVA-010.objective: Ensure that each assessment has an approved boundary (physical, logical, organisational, provider and temporal), applicable criteria (AIDCF artifact and capability-profile versions, applicable controls, claim types, gates), and visible exclusions with their residual effect.
MCF-EVA-010.requirement: The lead assessor shall prepare, and the decision authority shall approve before fieldwork, a scope record for each assessment stating the boundary across physical, logical, organisational, provider and temporal dimensions; the operating states assessed; the applicable AIDCF artifact and capability-profile versions; the applicable controls with claim types; the applicable gates; and every exclusion with rationale and residual effect on the decision. The lead assessor shall reconcile the boundary to the ArchitectureSnapshot (MCF-CAP-004) and record any element of the snapshot that is neither in scope nor excluded.
MCF-EVA-010.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: assessment boundary unresolved; CG-02 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE

MCF-EVA-011.objective: Ensure that sampling is risk-based, reproducible and not over-extrapolated, and that tests are authorised, safe, defined in advance (initial state, method, expected result, abort criteria, restoration) and recorded with anomalies.
MCF-EVA-011.requirement: The lead assessor shall document, for each sample, the population and its frame, strata, selection method, sample size rationale, exclusions and expansion rule, and shall record failed samples and their effect. For each test, the lead assessor shall obtain written authorisation from the system owner and, for hazardous or service-affecting tests, the safety authority, and shall record the initial state, method, expected result, abort criteria, instrumentation, restoration steps, result and anomalies. Tests shall be performed by authorised operators; assessors shall observe.
MCF-EVA-011.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected results may be over-extrapolated or unsafe to rely on; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

MCF-EVA-012.objective: Ensure that domain specialists (electrical, mechanical, compute, storage and network, OT security, resilience, evidence and data) approve the technical methods and conclusions in their domains, and that reliance on specialists is recorded with scope, competence and responsibility.
MCF-EVA-012.requirement: The lead assessor shall identify, for each assessment, the domains requiring specialist judgement, appoint a competent specialist for each (MCF-GOV-023), and record the specialist's scope, competence evidence and responsibility. Each specialist shall approve the methods and the Control Assessment results in their domain. Where a specialist is external, the lead assessor shall evaluate their independence and the transferability of their conclusions.
MCF-EVA-012.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected domain results carry CONF-2 ceiling and a decision condition

MCF-EVA-013.objective: Ensure that every Finding is traceable to the criterion, the evidenced condition, the supporting and challenging evidence, the affected Service Outcomes, controls and gates, and to its action and closure evidence.
MCF-EVA-013.requirement: The lead assessor shall record every Finding with a stable identifier, criterion (control and assessment criterion), condition, supporting and challenging Evidence Object references, cause where evidenced or labelled as analysis, consequence for Service Outcomes, dependencies and states, classification, and gate and score effect. The action owner shall record closure evidence, and the lead assessor shall close a Finding only after re-assessing that evidence.
MCF-EVA-013.unknownEffect: US3 Material: residual deficiency status uncertain; decision condition recorded

MCF-EVA-014.objective: Ensure that missing, inaccessible, stale, conflicting or unverifiable knowledge is recorded as an UNKNOWN Record with type, severity and decision effect, carried unchanged into gates, scores, decisions and reports, and never silently resolved favourably.
MCF-EVA-014.requirement: The lead assessor shall record every UNKNOWN as an UNKNOWN Record with subject, missing attribute, type (U1-U10), severity (US1-US5) with the test that determined it, reason, potential consequence, evidence needed, owner, status and gate and decision effect. The decision authority shall ensure that every US3, US4 and US5 UNKNOWN Record is reflected in the Gate Results, decision ceiling and report, and that UNKNOWN Records are closed only by new evidence or approved re-scoping, never by assumption.
MCF-EVA-014.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: the reliability of every Gate Result is in doubt; CG-12 evaluation cannot conclude and decisions are capped at LIMITED

MCF-EVA-015.objective: Ensure that when material evidence supports incompatible propositions (for example design shows 2N power, EPMS shows a shared upstream breaker), both lineages are preserved, the conflict is analysed and resolved, bounded or escalated, and the result reflects it.
MCF-EVA-015.requirement: The lead assessor shall register each material evidence conflict as an EvidenceConflict with both assertions and their evidence lineages, analyse scope, time and state differences, seek corroboration, obtain competent review and record whether the conflict is resolved, bounded or escalated. Unresolved conflicts shall be recorded as U4 UNKNOWN Records; observed or tested evidence shall take precedence over design intent unless shown to be unrepresentative.
MCF-EVA-015.unknownEffect: US3 Material: results may rest on contested evidence; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

MCF-EVA-016.objective: Ensure that every limitation on the conclusion (exclusions, restricted or inaccessible evidence, untested states, assumptions, sampling limits, provider reliance) is disclosed in every report and statement at a prominence matching its effect.
MCF-EVA-016.requirement: The lead assessor shall compile a limitations register for each assessment covering exclusions, restricted or inaccessible evidence, unassessed operating states, assumptions, sampling and test limits and reliance on providers or specialists, each with its effect on the decision. The reporting owner shall ensure every report and Assurance Statement for the assessment discloses each limitation with an effect on the decision, and that redaction for security does not remove a limitation.
MCF-EVA-016.unknownEffect: US3 Material: intended users may over-rely; decision condition recorded

MCF-EVA-017.objective: Ensure that, for each assessment, every critical gate CG-01 to CG-15 is determined as applicable or APPROVED_NA with boundary rationale, and that the CRITICAL and SUPPORTING control set for each applicable gate is identified from the registry for the scope.
MCF-EVA-017.requirement: The lead assessor shall determine, for each assessment, the applicability of each gate CG-01 to CG-15 to the decision question and boundary, shall identify for each applicable gate the in-scope CRITICAL and SUPPORTING controls from the AIDCF-007A registry gate mappings and the gate criteria from AIDCF-010, and shall submit any proposed APPROVED_NA with boundary rationale to the decision authority. Meta-gates CG-11 and CG-12 shall always be applicable.
MCF-EVA-017.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: affected Gate Results cannot be relied upon; decision capped at LIMITED

MCF-EVA-018.objective: Ensure that evidence for each applicable gate meets the gate's mandatory evidence classes and sufficiency floor from AIDCF-008, without substitution below the floor to complete a scorecard, and that Gate Results are computed by the AIDCF-010 roll-up rule.
MCF-EVA-018.requirement: The lead assessor shall assemble, for each applicable gate, a gate Evidence Package containing the mandatory evidence classes for that gate, shall assess its sufficiency against the gate floor, and shall compute the Gate Result by the AIDCF-010 roll-up rule from CRITICAL control results, gate criteria and evidence sufficiency. The independent reviewer shall confirm, for each gate, that no evidence below the mandatory type or quality floor was substituted.
MCF-EVA-018.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: Gate Results unverified; decision capped at LIMITED

MCF-EVA-019.objective: Ensure that the Assurance Decision is issued by the accountable decision authority, separate from those who prepared and performed the assessment, on the basis of a recorded Decision Recommendation and review, and that automation only proposes.
MCF-EVA-019.requirement: The decision authority shall issue each Assurance Decision personally or through documented delegation, on the basis of a Decision Recommendation from the lead assessor and the independent review record, and shall record the decision state, controlling reasons (including Gate Results and UNKNOWN ceilings), conditions with owners and dates, and validity. The tool owner shall ensure that no tool can transition a decision to APPROVED without the decision authority's authenticated action.
MCF-EVA-019.unknownEffect: US3 Material: decisions' authority uncertain; intended reliance restricted and condition recorded

MCF-EVA-020.objective: Ensure that reports and statements use only the controlled decision, gate and result vocabulary, bound every conclusion by Capability Instance, Service Outcomes, scope, states and date, and contain no prohibited claims.
MCF-EVA-020.requirement: The reporting owner shall ensure that every report and Assurance Statement uses the controlled decision states (REASONABLY_ASSURED, CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED, LIMITED, NOT_ASSURED, INCONCLUSIVE), Gate Results (PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN, APPROVED_NA, NOT_ASSESSED) and control results of AIDCF-010 with the controlled wording of AIDCF-012; bounds each conclusion by Capability Instance, Service Outcomes, boundary, operating states and as-of date; and contains no prohibited claim (certified, accredited, universally safe, secure or resilient, compliant with all laws). The independent reviewer shall check claim language before issue.
MCF-EVA-020.unknownEffect: US3 Material: external reliance may exceed decision; condition recorded

MCF-EVA-021.objective: Ensure that each Evidence Object relied on by a current decision has a currency basis and review date, that expiry is detected, and that expired mandatory evidence triggers review of the claims it supports.
MCF-EVA-021.requirement: The evidence lead shall record, for each Evidence Object supporting a current Assurance Decision, its currency basis and review date per AIDCF-008, shall monitor for expiry, and on expiry of mandatory evidence shall notify the lead assessor and capability owner, mark the evidence STALE and initiate review of the dependent claims and Gate Results within the expiry response time.
MCF-EVA-021.unknownEffect: US3 Material: current decisions may rely on stale evidence; condition recorded

MCF-EVA-022.objective: Ensure that material change, incidents, gate changes and evidence invalidation automatically or reliably trigger reassessment of the affected claims, gates and decisions, and that the trigger mechanism is shown to work.
MCF-EVA-022.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall define reassessment triggers for each current Assurance Decision (material architecture, capacity, configuration, provider or ownership change; incidents affecting Service Outcomes; gate FAIL or critical UNKNOWN; evidence invalidation), shall connect the change, incident and evidence systems so that trigger events are routed to the lead assessor and capability owner, and shall verify at least once per trigger test interval, by injecting a test event, that triggers reach the responsible roles and initiate reassessment.
MCF-EVA-022.unknownEffect: US3 Material: current decisions may persist after invalidating change; CG-14 evaluation records the gap

MCF-EVA-023.objective: Ensure that where continuing assurance is claimed, the specific claims monitored, the telemetry and evidence feeds used, their coverage and their blind spots are defined, and that feed health is itself monitored.
MCF-EVA-023.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall, for each claim under continuing assurance, define the monitored indicators, their source feeds, coverage across assets, locations and operating states, thresholds that trigger review, and known blind spots. The tool owner shall monitor feed health (gaps, latency, clock integrity, dropped data) and alert the evidence lead on degradation; the programme lead shall state blind spots in each continuing-assurance report.
MCF-EVA-023.unknownEffect: US3 Material: continuing-assurance claims unsupported; continuing claims reverted to point-in-time with condition

MCF-EVA-024.objective: Ensure that when a decision can no longer be relied upon (material change, incident, gate FAIL, evidence invalidation, expiry), it is suspended, withdrawn or superseded promptly, intended users are notified, and history is preserved, so that failure of a prior conclusion is contained.
MCF-EVA-024.requirement: The decision authority shall define criteria for suspension, withdrawal and supersession of Assurance Decisions, shall act on each trigger response that meets the criteria within the suspension time, shall notify all intended users and recipients of external communications, and shall preserve the prior decision, its evidence manifest and the reason for change. The programme lead shall rehearse the suspension and notification process at least once per rehearsal interval.
MCF-EVA-024.unknownEffect: US3 Material: reliance on invalid decisions may continue; condition recorded and current decisions reviewed
